decklists.name: Phase, Daze, Repeat!
decklists.description_md:
Shadowcat excels in aggression and protection, both of which offer her ample opportunities to get into phased form for villain attacks. However, she can be quite good in justice too!

This is my attempt to build a deck for her in an aspect that is not considered optimal for her hero design. It is meant for 1-2 players, as it is an all-rounder and not a "turbo-thwart" justice deck that might be needed in higher player counts. It's performed quite well so far in standard and against Expert Crossbones (I am fairly new to MC, so not doing much expert games yet).

The premise of the deck is pretty straightforward, and is built around 3 design features:

1. Lots of confuses to allow you to flip down to avoid damage, heal, and switch forms if necessary. The confuses can help get a little bit of extra card draw with AE hand size and Kitty's Room. 

2. Extra attack cards to provide more opportunities to flip to phased form before the start of the villain phase.

3. Lots or readies to also help with form-flipping and to deal with minions/side schemes/etc. as needed. It also helps to mitigate stuns, which feel pretty awful for Kitty!

The deck has 7 confuses (phased and confused is a great card in this deck),  7 + readies (7 cards plus any readies from Utopia), and is an aggressive justice deck with stealth strikes and concussive blows augmenting Kitty's impressive attack cards.

Concussive blow works beautifully with Kitty's built-in resource generator, and Lay Down the Law is easy to get off with her frequent form flips.

Because she doesn't need to flip down too often, she can confuse the villain and take advantage of "Float Like a Butterfly" pretty easily. It works well with Shadowcat Surprise!

Kitty may shine in protection and aggression, but she's not to be underestimated in justice,

decklists.name: Drunken Master
decklists.description_md:
Updated list: [401421](https://marvelcdb.com/deck/view/401421) ![shadowcat](https://i.imgur.com/WzSroo8.jpg) *So* that's *why the rum's gone*

Ever feel like everything just goes your way, but you don't know why? [Ever wake up after a long night of drinking with even *more* money in your pockets, meaning you have traded goods **and/or** services for money?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XpPs665-q7o) Or maybe suffering from imposter syndrome? This is the deck for you. Get ready to stumble into greatness. Or don't. It'll happen anyway.

** Head Fu ** The first thing about [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) is that playing her revolves around getting the most out of [Solid](/card/32031a) / [Phased](/card/32031b). It's subtly different from other form changers like [Ant-Man](/card/12001a), [Wasp](/card/13001a), and even her closest analogue, [Vision](/card/26001a). Although understanding the card itself isn't all that difficult, there are some non-obvious implications: - [Solid](/card/32031a)'s flip response is not forced, so it is *always optional*. - [Phased](/card/32031b)'s flip response _is_ forced, so it is *always mandatory*. - Shadowcat's mass form upgrade can flip an unlimited number of times per round. - [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) will always trigger after [Phased](/card/32031b), since the latter is a forced response and the former is a regular response. - Playing [Defiance](/card/26018), [Preemptive Strike](/card/05014), or [Quick Shift](/card/32040) *always* counts as defending since you can only play it during an attack. This also always makes you the defender of that attack, whether your used your basic action to defend or not. - [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) is an easy way to interrupt an attack and switch to the appropriate form. It additionally redirects attacks towards you and counts as defending (and attacking) even if you have not used your basic defense action. It does ~~not~~ trigger [Solid](/card/32031a) / [Phased](/card/32031b) more than once since it is simultaneously an Attack and Defense in the same action. ~~What is unclear based on the rulings is that, since it fully resolves before the attack, you should still resolve the flip after defending the attack as normal, but I think we're still awaiting clarification on that.~~ They have finally ruled that if you are in PHASED when you play it, you will be in SOLID for the attack, and if you are SOLID when you play it, you have the option (and you should) flip to PHASED for the attack. Since it is a defense event, you will then have the option at the end of the attack to flip again (if solid) and forced to flip (if phased). - [Side Step](/card/14015) can trigger during an undefended attack initiated against Shadowcat, declaring her the defender. If playing while in [Phased](/card/32031b), the damage prevention of Phased triggers, preventing all damage instead of just 3. - SC0E has a very helpful [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2431JkwTEqY) explaining a lot of this, and he's a great dude, so give it a watch. ** Stumbling Into Greatness ** The basic strategy of this deck is just defend a lot and win. It's so easy a drunkard can do it, so pour your favourite drink and get dodging. Drunken fighters always win. Thwart your enemies' plans, turn their attacks against themselves, and get drunk. Life's a party, and you're here to have a good time. Ok, let's get into it.

![drunken master](https://media.tenor.com/MqY82Rxw6bMAAAAd/rock-lee-kimimaro.gif)

** Take a Swig ** Most Protection thwarting options are highly vulnerable to side schemes. Thankfully, [Shadowcat](/card/32030a)'s ability can completely bypass it, but it requires some finesse due to the timing of [Solid](/card/32031a) / [Phased](/card/32031b) flipping if you also want to avoid all damage. To assist with thwarting, your first options are your [designated drinking buddy](/card/32032) and [Airwalk](/card/32039). [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) additionally helps with confusing the villain, but be sure to line this up with a minion attack you can defend against, otherwise you will lose your normal defensive triggers. [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017) removes main scheme threat after defending. Howver, if you defend while in Solid, you can flip to Phased instantly and trigger the effects, ignoring any in play. If you defend in Phased, you have to flip to Solid first, so it won't bypass crisis anymore. With [Intangible Interference](/card/32035), you can additionally help clear that side scheme at the same time. But you want to defend in your [drunken stupor](/card/32031b), but thankfully there's a nice combo piece: [Counter-Punch](/card/01077). Here's the sequence: - Defend against an attack while in [Phased](/card/32031b) - Immediately after the attack resolves, you must resolve [Phased](/card/32031b)'s forced response and flip back to [Solid](/card/32031a) - Since [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) has the same triggering condition, you can also choose to resolve this before choosing to trigger [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017), switching back to [Phased](/card/32031b) - Et voila! Have another drink, you've earned it! \**Hic*\*

** Head of Stone ** The best part of drunken martial arts is having your enemy do all the work for you, leaving you more time to drink. Just sit back, drink, and let your enemies punch themselves. [Counter-Punch](/card/01077), [Powerful Punch](/card/32014), and [Preemptive Strike](/card/05014) can only be used before (if it's an interrupt) or after (if it's a response) an enemy attack. [Side Step](/card/14015) is unique in that it can be played any time you would take damage, even outside of an attack. If you are the target of an undefended attack, it will declare you the defender, and if in [Phased](/card/32031b), will prevent all damage. [Electrostatic Armor](/card/10031), and [Flow Like Water](/card/26016) double down on this, triggering bonus additional damage every attack. Keep in mind that [Electrostatic Armor](/card/10031) can only trigger once per attack (regardless of how many defense events you play), while [Flow Like Water](/card/26016) triggers every time you play a defense event, which can trigger multiple times per attack (and even outside of attacks, so long as you have met their triggering conditions). Outside of that, [Lockheed](/card/32032), [Phase Strike](/card/32038) and [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) can help put even more pressure on the opponent. [Acute Control](/card/32034) can occasionally pull work against Guard minions while keeping pressure on the villain. Keep in mind that you still cannot play [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) on the villain after defending from [Phased](/card/32031b) while engaged with a Guard minion, since it will flip to [Solid](/card/32031a) before you can trigger [Counter-Punch](/card/01077). Similarly, defending while in [Solid](/card/32031a) and using [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) on the villain will be stopped by a Guard minion.

** Liquid Courage ** Alcohol's final benefit is the ability to ignore an enormous amount of pain. [Phased](/card/32031b) is the primary method of ignore damage, and you have many ways to phase out and have yourself another drink uninterrupted. [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) and [Quick Shift](/card/32040) can all be used before attacks to flip to [Phased](/card/32031b) if they would initiate while you are in [Solid](/card/32031a). [Defiance](/card/26018), [Preemptive Strike](/card/05014), [Side Step](/card/14015), and defending normally can be used mid-attack for the same result. And finally, [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) can help after attacks to help set up for the next one. [Defiance](/card/26018) and [Preemptive Strike](/card/05014) have an additional benefit of being able to work with your DEF to help prevent as much damage as possible while defending in [Solid](/card/32031a).

** Raid the Cabinet ** When you need to restock for the next beer run, there are plenty of ways to chip in. [Defensive Energy](/card/32018) is one of the best, paying for [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) and [Preemptive Strike](/card/05014) and drawing an additional card. [Kitty's Room](/card/32033) draws additional cards while in Alter-Ego, [Deft Focus](/card/16024) discounts most of your own cards (seriously, almost everything is a superpower). [Nerves of Steel](/card/14017) pays for [Powerful Punch](/card/32014), [Preemptive Strike](/card/05014), and [Side Step](/card/14015), additionally paying the correct resource type for [Side Step](/card/14015)'s kicker. [Unflappable](/card/09020) is seriously easy to trigger, drawing an addition card every round. And finally, [Solid](/card/32031a) has a every round for any Attack or Defense event. Once you have [Nerves of Steel](/card/14017) down, you can save Solid for mostly your Attack events, [Phase Strike](/card/32038) and [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037). If you are paying for multiple Defense events, of course utilise it. There are plenty of both to get _solid_ returns from [Solid](/card/32031a) (ayy). UPDATE: In the most recent version of the deck, A few cards have ben removed to make room for some shiny new tools. [Change of Fortune](/card/48014) helps you draw up to 3 extra cards per turn with [Unflappable](/card/09020); goodbye [Assess the Situation](/card/12033). [Taunt](/card/42016) lets you get immediate value from Defense events already in hand and [Nerves of Steel](/card/14017) and helps draw you more cards. Now you can go more rounds with the villain and still pump out lots of value during the player phase. So get out there, get drunk, and win. What more is there? ![hold fast](https://i.pinimg.com/736x/7f/da/ba/7fdabaeba3576680a6fe23d5b53502bb.jpg)

Player Count: All
Key Cards: Lockheed, Danger Room

![Toothless](https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/How-to.jpg)
## Let’s Do Something Stupid
So…ngl…I just saw the live-action How to Train Your Dragon, and it was such a good movie. I couldn’t help but wonder how I could use the (currently) only playable dragon and have fun. At first, I thought about just Sidekicking and Voltroning [Lockheed](/card/32032) and disregarding the powerful “enters play” effect. That had too many feel-bad moments and felt unthematic to the movie. So then, it quickly became how do I recur Lockheed as much as possible and get a Training card on him without paying for it. 

## So Let’s Do Something Crazy
So this deck aims to help you get [Danger Room](/card/33021) out quickly so you can use it to train your dragon! Then, keep recurring that dragon. There are plenty of times to flip down, call your Dragon, train it, and clear the main scheme or do some damage. You can be recurring this dragon 4 or 5 times in the course of a game.

How do we get Danger Room out quickly? Mulligan hard for [Danger Room](/card/33021), [Forge](/card/36022), or [Build Support](/card/40027). You can generally get one of those within two turns. Then, find your dragon and go!

## Gestured to All of Me
Well, once we get our Dragon Training Engine going, what else matters? A couple of Shadowcat tenets still hold true, it’s always worth it to make sure you end your turns in Phased to get the full defense for yourself. [Deft Focus](/card/49023) and [Solid](/card/32031a) can help make sure you pay for Shadowcat’s cards. (You are flipping down enough to include [X-Gene](/card/38019) if you wanted, but I wasn't getting enough mileage to include it). 

With that, the game is done. It just takes some time. As far as pacing, in solo, standard should take you 1-1.5 deck passes, and in expert, it should be 2-2.5 deck passes. That’s not a hard and fast rule, but it can help you judge if you’re pacing this deck correctly on average.

---
### Sideboard
**Current Environment**:
- 1x [Clarity of Purpose](/card/31029) —> 1x [X-Gene](/card/38019)

---
### Check Out these Other Decks
Here are some decks that can go along well with this deck.
- Aggression: [Angel’s Aerial Children of the Atom](https://marvelcdb.com/decklist/view/50392/angel-s-aerial-children-of-the-atom-1.0) by [NickE81](https://marvelcdb.com/user/profile/47842/NickE81)
- Justice: [Colossal Gunboat](https://marvelcdb.com/decklist/view/43240/colossal-gunboat-1.0) by [Castlefrank47](https://marvelcdb.com/user/profile/19491/Castlefrank47)
- Protection: [Get This Villain a Shield](https://marvelcdb.com/decklist/view/49272/get-this-villain-a-shield-2.0) by [MrSelfDestruct](https://marvelcdb.com/user/profile/34910/MrSelfDestruct)

decklists.name: Shadowcat Goes All Out
decklists.description_md:
![Shadowcat Goes All OUT](https://i.pinimg.com/736x/aa/31/55/aa3155805c4e01bfdacfcf44058b8e77.jpg)

Check out the deck vs. Expert Juggernaut: https://youtu.be/kFkV9UG534c

# Shadowcat Goes All Out

Well, you guessed it, the theme card for this deck is [Go All Out](/card/29017). Strange how there is only 2 copies of the card in this deck.... hmmm.

## How's it is meant to be played

Step 1: GET DOWN RESOURCE GENERATORS STAT. [The X-Jet](/card/36023) and [Helicarrier](/card/01092) are your absolute best friends. [Solid](/card/32031a) is not going to be super helpful in building out. [Avengers Mansion](/card/01091), [Kitty's Room](/card/32033) and [Moira MacTaggert](/card/38018) will all be additionally helpful in drawing cards. 

Step 2: GET SET UP. You'll want to get [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022) to prepare and make sure [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) is queued up also. 

Step 3: BUILD UP. This is where you'll get ready for [Go All Out](/card/29017). Play [Morale Boost](/card/05032) whenever you can to buff your stats a bit and whenever you change forms hit up [Moxie](/card/12016) to buff your stats more. For good measure throw down a [Lead from the Front](/card/01070), especially if you have some allies in play. Then with a [Go All Out](/card/29017) hit the villain for a potential of 14pts of damage! (can be more if you play your cards right!)

## Allies

Allies are not essential, but incredibly helpful. [Beast](/card/33011) has always got your back with an additional resource card. [Cyclops](/card/49015) will help you with some extra damage when you need it. [Pixie](/card/36017) will grab you an extra card or a solid ally to play. [Kid Omega](/card/49013) is a great cheap ally to play alongside [Lockheed](/card/32032) to get some bonus threat and damage. 

Check out the deck against expert Juggernaut: https://youtu.be/kFkV9UG534c

As always, let me know what you guys think and it always helps if you drop a like and a comment :)

decklists.name: Kitty Surprise (Attack)
decklists.description_md: _**One of my favorite MC players explains Shadowcat in a very informative video:**_ [SC0E HOW TO: Shadowcat!](http://https://youtu.be/2431JkwTEqY) ________ _(I've completed all of Mutant Genesis multiple times on Expert with variations of this deck. Turns out Shadowcat is very strong and really has an answer for everything. The form mechanic, which [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) exploits, is probably the most well-designed. Not only is she super powerful, but she's quite engaging and very fun to play!)_ _________ ### **_Synopsis:_** - [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) is probably best used by Shadowcat better than any other hero because she flips so easily. I've tried Shadowcat in all aspects and I really enjoy this one the most based on how much control you feel you have to flip your Mass form. This is really important for so many of her cards: [Lockheed](/card/32032), [Airwalk](/card/32039), [Phase Strike](/card/32038), etc. - This deck uses [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) to flip to control your Mass Form and ensure you always get to use your Solid resource to great effect, while also defending and taking no damage. You can do this multiple times in a turn if you have the right cards in hand. - This ensures that you’ll almost always be able to end up in Phased form during the villain phase so you can defend without taking damage. This is very important if you have [Quick Shift](/card/32040), for example. - You always get to use Surprise Attack’s kicker because of the on Solid Form -- 4 damage essentially for the 1 ER. - Killing a minion after you block the villain’s attack using [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) and killing a minion on the board before they even get to attack –- is there a more satisfying play?! ___ ### **_Typical Play:_** - Play [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) if you have it, this is very, very good value and also stacks with the stun of [Drop Kick](/card/10014). You should be able to really slow down the villain with these cards. - On your turn, always think about how to end up in Phased form using the on Solid form. That means using the attack events to end up in the correct form. - On the villains turn, you should be in Phased form. Of course, play [Quick Shift](/card/32040) to defend without exhausting if you have it and take zero damage. Side note: I actually always hold on to [Quick Shift](/card/32040) if I have it no matter what. I rarely do this with defense cards. - Then, if you don't need [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) on your turn or you expect another attack that you need to defend, use it on the villain phase to flip immediately back from Solid form (use the ) and flip back to Phased once again to defend and take zero damage again. ___ ### **_Cards/Combos:_** - [Phased](/card/32031b) + [Martial Prowess](/card/10018) + [The X-Jet](/card/32020) = 3 for [Drop Kick](/card/10014) - [Wolverine](/card/32041) is a powerful ally to get rid of all the Tough in Mutant Genesis. - [Deft Focus](/card/16024) has a lot of Shadowcat targets: [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037), [Airwalk](/card/32039), [Intangible Interference](/card/32035), [Acute Control](/card/32034), & [Phase Strike](/card/32038). - [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022) is essentially a 1-cost ready that you can easily use on any turn. Again, I think Shadowcat uses this card better than anyone. You can also use this card to again flip to the form you need to end up in. - [Utopia](/card/33020) can help you ready when you had to actually exhaust to defend with no [Quick Shift](/card/32040). This can be really useful in scenarios like Sabretooth where you have to protect [Robert Kelly](/card/32066). ___ ### **_Stun/Confuse/Tough:_** - I think this deck will change over time, for example there is a certain Aggression ally that will come out soon that has been spoiled that I would add when she comes out -> https://hallofheroeslcg.com/logan-wolverine/#jp-carousel-16200. - [Drop Kick](/card/10014)/[Professor X](/card/32019) – I know there’s bound to be some questioning of these cards due to the Steady/Stalwart in Mutant Genesis. But I feel that it's quite overblown as much of it can be removed and often you almost have to have status effects in some scenarios. With the on Solid form, [Martial Prowess](/card/10018) and [The X-Jet](/card/32020) it's easy to get the kicker. Mutant Genesis also has minions with a lot of hit points that now offer good targets for when the villain does happen to have immunity. - Another thing you might notice is that Mutant Genesis has a lot of Tough! Therefore when you go up against Master Mold for example, you can always use [Piercing Strike](/card/04044) to help with all the Tough. ___ ### **_Other Card Options:_** - I've played many variations of this deck. I think a lot of the time each version has worked better dependent on scenario. I've played versions with/without: - Adding: 1. [Clobber](/card/18012) for more events and for [Drop Kick](/card/10014) 2. [Piercing Strike](/card/04044) 3. [Assault Training](/card/26033) - Subtracting: 1. [Shadow and Steel](/card/32021) 2. [Boot Camp](/card/13016) 3. [Team-Building Exercise](/card/12024) ___

decklists.name: Who's Hiding?
decklists.description_md: This is my second Mutant Genesis hero deck using only X-Men and Core Set cards, geared towards new players. Next up we have Shadowcat. Her main gimmick is that, naturally, she's untouchable. If she's phased out and defending from an attack, she can't take any damage at all. So of course her preconstructed deck synergizes with this, right? Well, no. First off, it shares a similar problem to Colossus's; four allies and you can only play three if you're teamed up with the hero Colossus. It's hard to find a use for your Training cards, and it's especially difficult to use [Team Strike](/card/32045), which is a problem when it's one of the only attacks in your deck. And the other one is [Toe to Toe](/card/10015), a card that outright interferes with your gameplan of not getting hit. So, while we could switch out our attacks for more versatile ones, we can also change gears entirely. If Colossus doesn't want those Protection cards of his, let's borrow them. Now we have plenty of ways to attack via [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) and [Powerful Punch](/card/32014). Play a Counter-Punch after defending, and then use [Indomitable](/card/01082) or [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022) to ready up and defend again. All the ready effects are very helpful too; if you need to get into Phased form you can use your basic attack, otherwise you can use your basic thwart. But sometimes you're exhausted for other reasons and don't have an easy way to get back to Phased. For a time like that, there's always good old [Haymaker](/card/01087). And [Powerful Punch](/card/32014), as per my understanding of the rules, is an all-star; you can play it in Solid Form (using your Solid resource to help pay for it) and attack the villain for 4, then, since you attacked, you flip to Phased. Now, since it's also a Defense card, the villain is attacking you, and since you're defending the attack, you'll take no damage and flip back down to Solid. Solid all around. And if all that's still not enough you can play [Perseverance](/card/13033) any time you change through your Solid/Phased forms. If you like being invincible you'll probably love this deck. Big thanks to royal7 from Discord for coming up with the concept for these decks.

decklists.name: Kitty Pryde: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D.
decklists.description_md:
![Kitty Pryde: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D.](https://cdn.marvel.com/u/prod/marvel/i/mg/f/70/622a10d453631/standard_incredible.jpg)

Kitty Pryde is called in by S.H.I.E.L.D. to investigate a virus that has infected the Helicarrier's computer. As Shadowcat she's packing a Sonic Rifle to confuse the villain on top of her Dazed and Confused card. This enables her to bring Scare Tactics and Swift Retribution to deal more consistent damage to the villain. Supported by a team of experienced agents, Agent Coulson sets up either a Sting Operation to easily eliminate non-elite minions or focus on the main threat with Counterintelligence; Monica Chang brings the three Surveillance Teams to sweep the area for threat; Spider-Woman simply swings in, sometimes for free if the villain and multiple minions are confused, to clean-up and protect Shadowcat; and Quake...quakes. Finally, this squad can lockdown lethal minions in The Raft.

This deck is purely for theme as I've been looking at Marvel comics properties to bring in to Marvel Champions. I've played it once, true solo against Rhino on standard, for a single win. I've had trouble piloting Shadowcat outside of Aggression due to timing her mass form upgrade so as to both prevent damage and have the attack resource generator available at the right times. This led to scouring aspects for low-cost attack events, like Scare Tactics and Swift Retribution in Justice.

If I were going to exceed the 40 card threshold, I'd add three copies of Homeland Intervention to extend the life of the allies and Surveillance Teams, though I didn't really have an issue keeping threat under control in my first play. Another solid addition would be X-Gene to generate resources for her identity-specific events. I wouldn't include the X-Jet just because I think it breaks the theme. This isn't an X-Men deck, it's Kitty Pryde: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D.

decklists.name: The Mutant Genesis | Shadowcat, Tiny, but Fierce
decklists.description_md:
## The Mutant Genesis

>This is a set of eight hero decks from Mutant Genesis / Wave 6. These eight decks only require one Core Set, the Mutant Genesis Expansion box, and the six Wave 6 Hero packs. All eight can be built at once, and can be mixed and matched for multi-player games.

I learned a very valuable lesson from Sentinels of the Multiverse. Well, two lessons, if you include that I absolutely love superhero-themed, card-based, cooperative games that can also be played solo. The main lesson was this: **_Do not try to haul the entire collection to game night._** More relevant to Marvel Champions - **_Never do deck building at game night._**

Marvel Champions had just hooked me; I enjoyed playing it two-handed solo and wanted to try it out with my weekly gaming group. With these lessons in mind, I approached deckbuilding a little differently with Mutant Genesis and the accompanying wave of mutants. Armed with only a Core Set, Mutant Genesis, and the Wave 6 Hero packs, I constructed a series of grab-and-play decks that could be used interchangeably for 2-4 players (Probably solo, too, but I never tested them). These decks were tested against the Mutant Genesis Campaign, and all of the decks were successful in their pairings.

![Shadowcat](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/marveldatabase/images/0/03/Katherine_Pryde_%28Earth-616%29_from_Marvel_Universe_Cards_Series_I_0001.jpg)

# Shadowcat, Tiny, but Fierce

This Shadowcat deck sticks with its precon-suggested Aggression aspect. It focuses on combat tempo, sustained and burst damage, and survivability by focusing on efficient use of her **Mass Forms**, [Solid & Phased](/card/32031a). This Shadowcat deck is a hard-hitting aggression deck that deals a lot of damage, while leaving Shadowcat largely untouched.

## The Mass Form Card

The key to Shadowcat's ability to damage enemies and remain largely untouched is a comprehensive understanding of the intricacies of her Mass Form card. There are a few key concepts that must be internalized to take advantage of this powerful upgrade fully:

* When in **Phased** Mass Form, the flip ability is a **_Forced Response_**, meaning you **_MUST_** flip to **Solid** Mass Form.

* When in **Solid** Mass Form, the flip ability is a **_Response_**, meaning you **_MAY_** flip to **Phased** Mass Form.

* **_Attack_** & **_Defend_** are not limited to Basic Attacks and Defenses, but also apply to Events that are labeled **_Attack_** and/or **_Defend_**

* Cards like [Toe to Toe](/card/32046) have the opportunity to switch your mass form multiple times, once for the potential defense in response to the enemy attack, and once for the attack that deals 5 damage.

* It is key for Shadowcat's survivability to end the turn in **Phased** Mass Form. Remember, you don't *have* to change form every time you use an attack ability.

* Exhausting **Solid** Mass Form for the **_Resource_** ability does not prevent you from changing forms. Switching Mass Forms does *not* ready **Solid** Mass Form, and does *not* allow you extra uses of the **_Resource_** ability.

* You have to be **_Defending_** to take advantage of Shadowcat's **Phased** Mass Form's damage reduction. Undefended enemy attacks in **Phased** Mass form will deal damage.

Now that that is out of the way, let's get to the good stuff.

## Strike Hard, Strike Fast, No Mercy

This Shadowcat deck is pure Aggression. Build out a stable of hard-hitting allies such as [Colossus](/card/32048), [Wolverine](/card/32041), and [Magik](/card/32042) and start smashing. Buff one or more with [Attack Training](/card/32043) and a [Combat Training](/card/01057) for yourself. Then [Team Strike](/card/32045).

[Team Strike](/card/32045) is the All-Star in this deck, because it does several essential things:
* Big Damage - a fully developed [Team Strike](/card/32045) can do 13 damage for 2 ER, potentially even more if the other players at the table are playing **X-Men**
* Efficient damage distribution - you can assign all of the damage any way you need to.
* No Consequential damage - you get to attack with all of your allies and keep them healthy.
* Provides a respite for [Wolverine](/card/32041) - It will help him stay on the board longer, allowing him to do even more damage.

Take advantage of the **Phased** Mass Form to play [Toe to Toe](/card/32046) without downside. [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) and [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) provide you with extra readies to keep the attacks going. You'll want to play [Phase Strike](/card/32038) either in **Solid**, to take advantage of the resource Solid provides, or pay the extra resource in **Phased** to remove one of those pesky Villain Attachments (there are a lot in the Mutant Genesis scenarios!)

Shadowcat's kit cards, like [Acute Control](/card/32034) and [Intangible Interference](/card/32035), are situational but have the opportunity to make her actions while **Phased** more efficient. [Quick Shift](/card/32040) is helpful to make sure you're in the correct phase when you're attacked, or it can reward you if you're already in the proper phase. [Kitty's Room](/card/32033) can provide chip healing or a bonus draw, for those times when you have to flip down to avoid taking damage.

### The Mutant Genesis Deck Lists

decklists.name: Protecting shouldn't be so exhausting!
decklists.description_md:
__Protecting shouldn't be so exhausting!__
The idea behind this deck is being in Phased form going into the villain phase and using ___DEFENSE___ events which don't cause you to basic defend. This ensures you won't take any damage, you'll always be able to trigger [Unflappable](/card/09020), and you won't be exhausted going into the hero phase.
See it in action __here__ against Expert Morlock Siege! __And why is it so important to defend without exhausting? Because defending in Phased form forces you to flip to Solid form, and the easiest way back to Phased it to make a Basic attack, which you can't do if you're exhausted!__
* [Jump Flip](/card/27014)'s "prevent 2 damage" is "prevent all damage" while you're phased (and you can remove 2 threat from the main even if there's a Crisis icon because Shadowcat ignores Crisis while she's Phased)... * [Side Step](/card/26019)'s "prevent 3" is also "prevent all" * [Defiance](/card/26018) is the obvious 0-cost way to defend * [Quick Shift](/card/32040) is another great 0-cost ___DEFENSE___, and explain my thoughts about it in the next section * I have a whole section about [Preemptive Strike](/card/05014) too!
__Quick Shift__ [Quick Shift](/card/32040) is a card I was "wrong" about in the past. My feeling was that I only wanted to play it in Phased form to draw two cards, but now I think it's "better" (or at least "as good") to play it in Solid form because it's an interrupt which flips you to phased, where you'll take no damage because you're now defending. The villain attacks and you defend with an event and take no damage, but it flips you to Solid form. The Encounter card is [Assault](/card/01187) (or similar), so you defend with [Quick Shift](/card/32040) to get back to Phased and take no damage.
__Preemptive Strike__ [Preemptive Strike](/card/05014) is the only event that doesn't guarantee the ___DEFENSE___ and 0 damage because the villain might reveal a boost card with no boost! If this is in my hand I hope to have a different one as well just in case, but if a boost IS drawn I'll definitely use this even if the boost is only 1 because it also does some damage and I don't want to waste an opportunity when I _could_ have played it. I'll pull ___any___ other ___DEFENSE___ event with [Jocasta](/card/26013) because all others are guaranteed to get you the defense regardless of how many boost icons are (or would be) drawn. So maybe trade them out for [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017)?? _Maybe_, and I might do so after testing. __EDIT:__ I did NOT trade these after testing because of scenarios in which the villain attacks someone other than you! This can still trigger the _defense_ and no damage, while making you the defender without exhausting.
__ Energy __ [Jump Flip](/card/27014) and [Side Step](/card/14015) are slightly better when you pay for them with , so I've included some cards to help ensure that: * [Defensive Energy](/card/32018) is and also draws you a card * [The X-Jet](/card/32020) is generates * Of course, many of the events have an too, but I hate paying for a ___DEFENSE___ event WITH a ___DEFENSE___ event!

decklists.name: Shadowcat's Pirate Phase
decklists.description_md:
TLDR for solo players: Deck is intended for multiplayer, but check out the solo version at the end of the article for a modified solo version!

![](https://i.imgur.com/5s6LrJj.png)

## The New Hotness

**[Gunboat Diplomacy](/card/48032)** is a card that's become very popular, especially after we got **[Children of the Atom](/card/49037)**. I think its a really **Solid** card, and its not just a passing **Phase**. But after playing with it now in over a dozen decks, I've noticed that it has a pretty common weakness. The damage and thwarting it does can be disrupted very easily. It's susceptible to stun, confuse, guard, patrol, AND crisis! 

Here is where Shadowcat comes in. While in **Phased** form, we can just bypass guard, patrol, and crisis. And when you don't need to do that, we can play **[Gunboat Diplomacy](/card/48032)** for free in **Solid** form.

## A Ghost Ship with No Crew

Okay, okay. That's all well and good, you say. But who's steering this damned ghost ship??? There's no allies besides **[ol' Lizardbreath](/card/32032)** here, and he barely passes as a powder monkey (no offense). Here's the thing. **[Gunboat Diplomacy](/card/48032)** is an **Alliance** card. The cost of these cards are intended to be shared by the group, as a team. Part of the cost of this card is exhausting the 2 characters. So we will be relying on other players here. Shadowcat doesn't need allies, and other heroes can get higher thwart numbers than her, so it only makes sense.

## Finding that Crew
At the bare minimum, you just need an X-Men or X-Force teammate who is willing to contribute their basic activation for **[Gunboat](/card/48032)**. You can play **[CotA](/card/49037)** on them so that they can fit either role, and **[Heroic Intuition](/card/01065)** to boost their THW. Even better is if they have some X- allies too. That would mean that your basic activation is freed up, so you can defend for yourself in phased form, or use your activation to clear stun or confused. If anyone brings some allies for **[Gunboat](/card/48032)**, you can bring some **[Mission Trainings](/card/34016)** too. You may not even need the **[Children of the Atom](/card/49037)** if they are bringing an X-alliance deck.

Some stand out heroes that you want to play with include: Psylocke, Phoenix, Cable, Storm, Cyclops, Rogue, X-23, and Nightcrawler. The 3 Psionic heroes can each get to 3 THW, and have access to **[Cerebro](/card/34022)** to find more crew members. Storm and Cyclops decks tend to want more X-men allies, and they have a solid 2 THW. Rogue can replay **[Gunboat](/card/48032)** with **[Superpower Adaptation](/card/38009)**, and can get to 3 THW with **[Rogue's Jacket](/card/38004)**. X-23 and Nightcrawler have 2 THW and can easily ready their hero. The **[Rogue](/card/48012)** ally is also a fantastic target. I did a lot of my testing of this deck with my Psylocke deck, **[5G Psionics](https://marvelcdb.com/decklist/view/45094/5g-psionics-1.0)**, which is a VERY strong combo.

## Wrapping Up

I did my testing against Stryfe and Project Wideawake, both expert. These are great match ups for the deck. They both have crisis icons, which Kitty was able to just ignore and still keep the main threat down. **[One Way or Another](/card/22015)** is great for getting more crisis side schemes in play, and **[Intangible Interference](/card/32035)** is a great card to deal with them. Even if the scenario doesn't have crisis icons, this deck is still worth running for her perfect defense while Phased form and ignoring any guard or patrol minions.

One issue with **[Gunboat](/card/48032)** in phased form is that since it is an attack, it flips you back to Solid. I haven't found this to be a big problem. You can either basic attack or use **[Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037)** to go back to phased, or use **[Quick Shift](/card/32040)**. But on the other hand, when you don't need to bypass crisis, guard, or patrol; using **[Gunboat](/card/48032)** to go back to Phased is actually really nice.

**Cut options:** 
- **[CotA](/card/49037)** can go down to 1 or 0 copies depending on what everyone is bringing.

- **[One Way or Another](/card/22015)** can go down to 2 or 1 copies depending on how many side schemes there are.

**Add ons:** 
- **[Lay Down the Law](/card/12031)** is a nice one for Shadowcat, since you can trigger this any time you change your form card (even on the villain phase). You can add on top, or replace **[Clear the Area](/card/04049)** with this if you'd like.
- **[Mission Training](/card/34016)** if someone has good ally targets for **[Gunboat](/card/48032)**
- **[Honorary X-Men](/card/33035)** if there's a really good non mutant target around.
- A 3rd **[Skilled Investigator](/card/04047)** in a 3 or 4 player game, if you have room for it.

I made a solo version below, which works well, but I'm more excited about the multiplayer version. There's just something about going into a game with just me and my pet dragon, trying to recruit players at the table into my pirate crew. 

![](https://i.imgur.com/VcwWTVF.png)

Solo version works pretty well in general, and is especially strong if you are using the Hope Summers mod set. I tested this solo vs Stryfe and it did great.

decklists.name: Iron Maiden
decklists.description_md:
**Unusual X-Men Decks: #1 - Iron Maiden** Shadowcat in Leadership is already strange, but Leadership with only two allies added? _Even weirder._ But all you really need is [Iron Man](/card/09039) - and you have an almost 80% chance to find him on Turn 1 thanks to [Call for Aid](/card/12015)! You provide the defense, [Iron Man](/card/09039) provides almost everything else. Upgrade him to the nines. Profit. Win. When fully upgraded, Iron Man is dealing 6 damage or 4 threat removal +1 damage every turn - and he loves [Game Time](/card/33022). _Pepper? Fired. Kitty? Hired!_
- **Get Up and Game! takes the Iron Maiden up against Venom! Check out the full video [here](https://youtu.be/W302QqK433U)!** - **And check out Night of the Living Card Game going up against Expert Absorbing Man [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eTs76o-FCn4&ab_channel=NightoftheLivingCardGame)!**
**Overview:** - **Archetype:** Voltron (_heavily upgrading an ally_) - **Difficulty:** Above Average - **Recommended Player Count:** Any (1-4) - **Ideal Aspect Partners:** Justice - **Ideal Hero Partners:** Anyone with fast/minimal setup (Nova, Gamora, Wolverine, etc!) - **Matchups to Avoid:** Scenarios which steal allies (Mysterio, Loki, etc)
**Strategy:** Mulligan aggressively for [Iron Man](/card/09039) or [Call for Aid](/card/12015) - and I mean aggressively. Ditch all 6 cards if you don't see either in your initial hand! Find him as fast as possible. (_And let's face it, Tony is probably at the bar._) Including 3x Call For Aid along with Iron Man himself, we have a 77.5% chance to get Iron Man on our first turn if we potentially mulligan everything. Then, assuming you go to hero form and stay there, a 90% chance to see him on Turn 2 and 96.5% chance to see him on Turn 3. Next, check the clock - it's [Game Time](/card/33022)! Make Iron Man an [Honorary X-Men](/card/33035) and give him some [Danger Room Training](/card/33015). This is your top priority - Game Time can effectively be a 0-cost card for 6 damage. Or 0-cost for 4 threat removal + 1 damage. ~~Heal~~ Repair Iron Man with [First Aid](/card/01086). [Innovation](/card/21058) is great for this too. Never let him be defeated. Keep an eye on where your First Aids are and moderate your use of him if you have to. Meanwhile, focus on defending with Shadowcat and, once Iron Man is in play, aim to end each turn in Phased form or with [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) in play. We run 3x Call for Aid, 3x Honorary X-Men, and 2x Danger Room Training. Why so many? To consistently get the deck online. Everything has to be played in the right order and this ups our odds of being able to do so quickly. Feed the spares to [Plan B](/card/27024) and [Machine Man](/card/26022). Because of the nature of playing and setting up Iron Man, this deck has a slight preference to avoid scenarios that start with multiple encounter cards in play. Also, watch out for modular sets like Enchantress, Whispers of Paranoia, and Mystique! They will steal your Iron Man. Or outright delete him. Be the bodyguard he deserves - during the game and when setting it up! Iron Man and Shadowcat can thwart well but are better at dealing damage between Solid, [Sidearm](/card/23035) and Power Gloves. This means they _prefer_ to have a Justice player in multiplayer - but will still do great with any aspects and in solo play!
**Mulligan Priorities:** - [Iron Man](/card/09039) - [Call for Aid](/card/12015) (if Iron man is NOT in hand) - [Honorary X-Men](/card/33035) (if Iron Man IS in hand)
**Other Tips:** - If [Plan B](/card/27024) is in play, [Machine Man](/card/26022) is lower priority - and vice versa. You won't often need two resource sinks. - Did you know you can overpay with [Innovation](/card/21058) and still get its effects? Even on a 0-cost card? Sometimes this is useful! - You still want to try and end every turn in Phased form like most Shadowcat decks. If you can't end in Phased but you have [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) in hand, playing it goes up in priority. You can also save the confuse from it on an earlier turn to duck into alter-ego. - If you get unlucky and see all your [Danger Room Training](/card/33015)s before getting Iron Man in play, once he is in play? You can use [Call for Aid](/card/12015) to reset your deck since there are no other Avengers - just make sure you can deal with the encounter card! - Use [Quick Shift](/card/32040). Every time. If both copies are still in your deck, Phased and Confused becomes a much lower priority (as it can prevent you playing Quick Shift, your best signature card). - [Iron Man](/card/09039) is expensive and will cost your whole turn. Try to play him as early as possible while you still have hp and the main scheme's threat threshold to play with. The turn you play him? A huge tempo loss. Every turn following that? Enormous tempo gains. - Throw a spare [Honorary X-Men](/card/33035) on yourself. It will thin your deck and +1 hp never hurts!
**Good luck!**

decklists.name: Shadowcat - Ready for justice!
decklists.description_md:
This is my take on Shadowcat. A jolly fun deck that is packed with nice synergies and you can get a lot done during the villain phase given it's a justice deck. Short write up down below. 

** **
**The Idea** 

The idea is to always start the villain phase in Phased form, negating the villain's first attack. 

Sit in hero form for most game and exhaust defend vs the villain in Phased form, clear threat with [Lay Down the Law](/card/12031), hit the villain and clear minions with [Turn the Tide](/card/15015), draw a card with [Skilled Investigator](/card/04047), ready with [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022) or [Justice Served](/card/22014), so you can exhaust attack during the hero phase to end up in Phased form again with ease. Rinse and repeat. 

During the hero phase you want to end up in Phased form eventually, the deck is therefore packed with ready cards since this deck doesn't have that many attack events, and you'll thus want that exhaust attack. 

** **
**The Strategy**

So yeah, the above section pretty much sums up the strategy. The deck is played as a control deck. Take your time, clear minions and threat while chipping away hp from the villain. You will of course take some damage from minions, and there will be cases when you can't end your turn in Phased form. But fret not, we're in luck. [Phased and Confused](/card/32036)+[Professor X](/card/37017) will give us plenty of room to flip and heal. 

The deck provides you with plenty of forward planning, because ending up in Phased form is essential. Should you attack or thwart with your hero exhaust? If you play [Turn the Tide](/card/15015) will it force you back in Solid form? 

I should also clarify that, if you're in phased form and you're able to defend > clear a scheme with [Lay Down the Law](/card/12031) into [Turn the Tide](/card/15015) > [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022)/[Justice Served](/card/22014), you'll end up in phased again and be ready for another villain attack right away in case you draw an activation encounter card. This is simply bonkers. 

Also, I wanna mention that holy hell, [Overwatch](/card/30019) is designed to be in a Shadowcat deck. Put it on the main scheme, play [One Way or Another](/card/22015), pick up a nasty side scheme with the crisis icon and completely obliterate the side scheme with a chunky thwart on the main scheme, triggering [Intangible Interference](/card/32035) as well. 

[Justice Served](/card/22014) is there to give you more flexibility, and help you end the turn in phased form.  

If you care for it, you could include [Dazzler](/card/37012) but I've found him redundant.

If you want more damage, let's say in a solo scenario I'd drop one [Lay Down the Law](/card/12031) for another [Turn the Tide](/card/15015). 

** **
**Final thoughts**

It fairs pretty well on expert level. Not much else to say, I enjoy this deck quite a lot. Hope you do as well. Cheers!

decklists.name: Nine Lives (Expert Ronan defeated!)
decklists.description_md:
<hr>
Shadowcat is an amazing hero who, in my opinion, is most powerful when played in the Protection aspect! If you haven't tried it, I recommend it! And if you have tried it, I ask you this: have you tried her in Protection with [Jocasta](/card/26013) to grab [Quick Shift](/card/32040)?

End the villain form in [Phased](/card/32031b), defend for cheap, and profit wildly from a guaranteed [Unflappable](/card/09020). Defeat the villain with [Electrostatic Armor](/card/10031) and [Flow Like Water](/card/26016) while Shadowcat's versatility covers board control!

_This deck is built for solo play and has defeated Expert Ronan._
<hr>
**If you like this deck, feel free to give it a ❤ ! Thank you so much!**
<hr>

<hr>
#### **Letting the Cat Out of the Bag** - Misconceptions
<hr>
I have seen talk about Shadowcat on multiple platforms that Shadowcat does not need allies or double resource cards. And, from a certain point of view, this is true - because she is a very powerful hero who can perform extremely well without them. However, just because she doesn't _need_ them doesn't mean she doesn't _want_ them.

**The Double Resource Cards** ([Energy](/card/01088), [Genius](/card/01089), [Strength](/card/01090))  
Most Shadowcat decks will usually have at least 12 cards that cost 2 or more. If having that many aspect cards of such a cost would normally justify the inclusion of the  Power of X resource cards, then having that many across aspect/basic/hero cards absolutely justifies the basic double resource cards. Especially with the amount of card draw Shadowcat has in Protection to help things line up!

**Shadowcat and Allies**
Similar to the double resource cards, Shadowcat doesn't _need_ allies. However, I again argue that she does want at least a couple - notably when played solo. For one, Protection lacks threat removal and allies can help provide it. [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017) is fantastic, and her 2 THW is usually good enough to handle the main scheme otherwise, but what happens when a nasty side scheme enters play with 5+ threat as is the case with many beyond Rise of Red Skull? If [Airwalk](/card/32039) isn't in your hand - and there are only two copies anyway - you could be in major trouble.

Allies like [Daredevil](/card/31014), [Black Widow](/card/01075) and [Jocasta](/card/26013) provide up to 4 threat removal when used twice to THW. [Jocasta](/card/26013) can also find [Quick Shift](/card/32040) and hold it, giving us a third use of [Quick Shift](/card/32040) per deck cycle most of the time and, in the "worst case", can simply hold [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) or [Defiance](/card/26018). And [Black Widow](/card/01075) can use her ability to help us dodge the worst side schemes in the first place, along with helping us avoid Kitty's crippling obligation, Shadow of the Past, etc!

They also provide an emergency block in case the villain activates multiple times or you want to stay readied to put out some extra damage instead!

<hr>
#### **A Cat Always Lands on its Feet** - Defense Events
<hr>
Why do I think Protection is Shadowcat's most powerful aspect? [Quick Shift](/card/32040) and [Defiance](/card/26018) prevent you from taking damage from an attack for 0-cost when you're [Phased](/card/32031b). [Quick Shift](/card/32040) even replaces itself and gives you an extra card! 

[Preemptive Strike](/card/05014) and [Side Step](/card/14015) stop an attack for 1-cost (2 effective resources), but also deal damage! These are back-ups to be used when your 0-cost options are not in hand - but are still excellent.

And [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) exists to cover your defense if the villain attacks twice, or - more likely - you have a minion out against you that you couldn't finish off on the previous turn with Protection's low damage output. It also helps if you ended your turn in the wrong form, though this should be extremely rare.

And then there's [Defensive Energy](/card/32018). Did you know you can spend [Defensive Energy](/card/32018) on a 0-cost card? You can overpay with it, helping you cycle through your deck for more options. Of course, if you have it in hand with a 1-cost defense event you should prioritize it there instead. Just make sure you spend it on something!

Between [Unflappable](/card/09020), [Defensive Energy](/card/32018) and [Quick Shift](/card/32040), you can often end the villain phase with at least as many cards as you started with! Sometimes more! All with no damage taken. It's extraordinarily efficient.
<hr>
#### **Look What the Cat Dragged In** - Allies in Detail
<hr>
We mostly covered the allies earlier, but here's a quick breakdown of each:

- [Lockheed](/card/32032) - 2-cost (3 effective resources) for up to 4 damage or threat removal, or 3 and a block. While blocks are worth less to Shadowcat, he's a great candidate to bring in, deal 3 damage or threat removal, and then keep on the board for an emergency.

- [Jocasta](/card/26013) - She is out best ally because she has the ability to hold our best card [Quick Shift](/card/32040). Holding a card is usually equivalent to reducing her cost by 1, but since Quick Shift draws us two cards, it roughly works out that she removes 2 threat and blocks 2 attacks for 1-cost (2 effective resources). And that's very, very good. You can also use her to hold [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) for emergencies or [Defiance](/card/26018) as the next-best option. Don't underestimate the android!

- [Black Widow](/card/01075) - An oft-forgotten ally, but extremely useful. There are some things Protection is just not equipped to deal with, and she helps us dodge them. Shadow of the Past and Advance are the obvious choices, but I've also found great use in trading away nasty side schemes or big minions that Protection is ill-equipped to deal with such as Mystique. Kitty's obligation isn't talked about much but is, in my opinion, far nastier than the average obligation. Spending 1 resource to avoid it? I'll always take that deal.

- [Daredevil](/card/01058) - Like the other Protection allies, Daredevil has 2 THW. But he's 1 cheaper with no strings attached. It's a little plain, but you can ignore his ability in most cases and just thwart away. Keep him in reserve with 1 hp to block in a pinch or, in the event of a tricky side scheme or Advance, thwart again.

<hr>
#### **Did Someone say Cat Nip?** - Upgrades/Supports
<hr>
The usual upgrades/supports are all here. [Unflappable](/card/09020), [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017) and [Deft Focus](/card/16024). It's hard to make a case for any kind of Shadowcat Protection deck not having these. They are excellent and are  your priorities when you mulligan!

[Plan B](/card/27024) provides damage on demand, something Protection lacks. So, while initially a 2 resource investment (1-cost + the card itself), playing this on a quiet turn really helps you deal with minions for the rest of the game and helps turn excess defense events into damage. Having this around as a permanent way to get damage is not to be underestimated.

While I'm not usually a huge fan of [Flow Like Water](/card/26016) and [Electrostatic Armor](/card/10031), Shadowcat's desire to play at least 1 defense event per turn combined with [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) as a tool against minions makes them especially worthwhile. With both of them, you're usually dealing 2 damage to the villain every turn - more if you trigger [Preemptive Strike](/card/05014) or [Side Step](/card/14015). This tends to make up almost 50% of my damage against villains, all for just doing what you want to do anyway. And it means that [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) effectively deals 6 damage to a minion when used to defend against one!

With a built-in resource generator in [Solid](/card/32031a), great value from [Deft Focus](/card/16024) and great card draw from [Unflappable](/card/09020), it's arguable whether she even needs another - but I have found [The X-Jet](/card/32020) to be useful. It can still be used like [Nerves of Steel](/card/14017), but can also help make your hero phase stronger if you instead defended with a 0-cost card as well as helping you deal with any encounter cards that demand a certain type of resource.

<hr>
#### **Cat Got Your Tongue?** - Shadowcat Help
<hr>
Shadowcat is, without a doubt, one of the trickiest heroes to play in all of Marvel Champions, up there in complexity with the likes of Nova and Adam Warlock. It's easy to get lose in the puzzle that is her form changing, and it's easy to forget how the attack and defend rules interact with either form.

Check out these great videos by the amazing SC0E for help on playing her!  
- [Shadowcat Xplained: Part 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2431JkwTEqY&t=4s&ab_channel=SC0E)
- [Shadowcat Xplained: Part 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=49K-SnyO65w&ab_channel=SC0E)  
  
<hr>
**Good luck and have fun!**
<hr>

decklists.name: Pshadowcat - Psynergy
decklists.description_md: Sometimes you come across a synergy that is cool, but not powerful enough to build a deck around. I bumped into one of those, and decided to build a deck around it anyway! [A](https://marvelcdb.com/decklist/view/23359/the-power-of-shadowcat-aggression-1.0) [couple](https://marvelcdb.com/decklist/view/35394/now-you-see-me-now-you-don-t-2.0) of deckbuilders have noticed that [Pulse Grenade](/card/17023) is a useful safety for Shadowcat, giving her an *attack* event she can keep in her back pocket to trigger at the end of the hero phase if she's at risk of ending her turn Solid and needs to phase. Two resources is a lot to pay for a single-use safety that doesn't even ready Shadowcat. Unfortunately, there are very few support or upgrade options which have *attack*-keyword activations - [Plasma Pistol](/card/20022) doesn't, for example, even though it clearly should. There are two re-usable attack events on Basic upgrades, however. The first one is [Telekinesis](/card/41033), which there is (unfortunately) no way of cheating into play for true solo Shadowcat due to [Superpower Training](/card/40059) being limited to character-specific cards. I'm definitely considering the possibilities for a two-handed pairing with Aggression Psylocke or Justice Phoenix. That leaves us with the one attack-on-a-stick that Shadowcat *can* play: *Aaah! A talking Psimitar!* [Psimitar](/card/40029) doesn't require you to be Psionic to play it, only that you play Psionic cards to trigger it. Bad news: you can't play any of the events, so no triggering it outside of the hero phase. Good news: There's four more Psionic allies in the Magneto pack, bringing the total psi X-Men you can play in Leadership up to seven, plus a handful more if you stretch to X-Force. And [Stepford Cuckoos](/card/45049) as a Psionic support. (There *should* be even more - [Cosmo](/card/17020) not being a psi is a travesty). From there, the deck *mostly* builds itself. I opted for an all X-Men suite just to get full benefit out of [Utopia](/card/33020) and [Uncanny X-Men](/card/36018). No [Make the Call](/card/01071) as you need to play the *card* for the Psimitar to trigger. It also doesn't trigger off [Rapid Response](/card/08031), but [Won't Stay Down](/card/49016) is so much slower and less efficient that Response is better even without the psynergy. [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051), as I have [previously noted](https://marvelcdb.com/decklist/view/45459/shadowcat-long-term-thinking-1.0), is so good with Shadowcat that three copies of it are always the first thing I put in her decks. So what does all this psynergy get you? A fairly basic minion swarm, honestly. I did say at the start that the effect isn't powerful enough to carry a deck on its own! With Psimitar and Utopia in play, the first ally you play in each turn readies you, lets you change mass forms via the attack trigger, and then potentially lets you change mass forms again if Shadowcat attacks. In practice I found that its main utility was being able to change mass forms if locked in Solid while exhausted after basic-defending. If you start the turn exhausted it also lets you ready->change forms->thwart with *Selective Intangibility*, which is useful reasonably often. Doing the math on how many times you'll change forms in each hero phase actually gets complicated (especially with [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051)s making things even more dynamic). I found that I was frequently getting the count wrong at the start of the turn and occasionally had to give myself a do-over to wind up where I wanted to be at the end of the phase. This is generally a sign that there's some power in there waiting to be untapped, I just need to get better at playing the deck to see if I can make it worth the opportunity cost of having the entire deck built around the gimmick.
