decklists.name: Liquid Shadow (Fluid Motion)
decklists.description_md:
<hr>
### **Liquid Shadow**
<hr>
Imagine a world where they release a hero with a turn 1 resource generator for attacks, takes care of their own defense by being practically indestructible, and comes with multiple readies that also serve as attacks to trigger [Fluid Motion](/card/28016).

Now imagine [Fluid Motion](/card/28016) just sitting there, waiting to be loved.

Enter Shadowcat, who can help pay for attacks with her Solid form, ignore enemy attacks with Phased, and has [Fluid Motion](/card/28016)'s favourite new friend: [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037). Did I mention she can ignore crisis and patrol + has one of the best thwarting events in the game, to help control threat until you're all set up to deal immense damage?

P.S. She's the best user of [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) in the game!

<hr>
**If you like this deck, feel free to give it a ❤ ! Thank you!**
<hr>
<hr>
#### **Cat Nip Carnage**
<hr>
Once you have all three [Fluid Motion](/card/28016)s in play along with [Combat Training](/card/01057), that's potentially 6 ATK if you can play three attacks per turn. 

...If you can play three attacks to activate your [Fluid Motion](/card/28016)s (which this deck easily can, with many cheap attacks/attacks that draw cards), and ready twice, that's 18 damage from her basic ATKs alone!

And if you've played three attacks before your basic attacking? You're looking at roughly 9 damage from that alone! 

All this means it's very easy to reach 15-30 damage every single turn!

<hr>
#### **Are You Ready to Rumble?**
<hr>
To benefit most from [Fluid Motion](/card/28016), you need to start the turn ready and able to basic attack. Of course, if the villain attacks you want to block it - but this deck has many efficient ways to do so without even needing to exhaust!
 
- [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) prevents TWO villain activations!
- [Mockingbird](/card/01083) and [Thor](/card/25013) each prevent TWO villain activations!
- [Quick Shift](/card/32040) blocks one villain activation and draws you juicy attack cards
- [Drop Kick](/card/10014) prevents one villain activation and draws you juicy attack cards

Factoring in all copies, that is a potential of 13 blocked attacks per deck cycle on a regular villain. 10 against a Steady villain. And 7 against a Stalwart villain. Whatever way you cut it, Shadowcat is almost always going to be ready to dish out some pumped-up [Fluid Motion](/card/28016) damage!

Of course, the villain could activate again through an encounter card or exhaust you, so you want to be able to ready. Also? The more you can ready, the more times you benefit from some pumped-up [Fluid Motion](/card/28016) damage!

- [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) both activates [Fluid Motion](/card/28016) and readies you to use the ATK boost from it!
- [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022) is a cheap solution to ready yourself up almost at will. Shadowcat is the best user of this card in the game!

That's 6 readies, and Ready to Rumble is bankable - meaning you can play it one turn, then trigger it on a turn where you know you can activate all three [Fluid Motion](/card/28016)s to maximize your damage!
<hr>
#### **Solo:**
<hr>
In solo, the ideal strategy with this deck is to begin the game by playing slow, building up your [Fluid Motion](/card/28016)s and a [Combat Training](/card/01057) while keeping the threat under control with [Airwalk](/card/32039), [Lockheed](/card/32032) and your basic THW. After a few turns, once you are reasonably well set up you can flip the switch and start to race down the villain! Slow to start, quick to finish.
<hr>
#### **Multiplayer:**
<hr>
In multiplayer, your primary job is to clear minions for multiple players. With this in mind, you can start to mix in more damage while you build, taking advantage of your upgrades much earlier. Once you have 2-3 boosts to your basic ATK and either [Martial Prowess](/card/10018) or [Deft Focus](/card/16024) on the board, you'll start to find damage just naturally overflows onto the villain.

You should also consider swapping 3x [Press the Advantage](/card/04043) for 3x [One by One](/card/28014) at 3-4 player, or at 2-player in minion-heavy scenarios!
<hr>
#### **Mulligan:**
<hr>
The ideal cards to have at the start of turn 1 are: [Martial Prowess](/card/10018), [Fluid Motion](/card/28016), [Deft Focus](/card/16024) and [Combat Training](/card/01057).

<hr>
### **Tips and Tricks**
<hr>
- Solid form helps meet the physical requirement on [Drop Kick](/card/10014) and [Surprise Attack](/card/13014). If you have one of these in hand, try to save Solid form's resource generator to use on them!

- [Fluid Motion](/card/28016)'s damage boost only lasts until the end of a phase! Don't use [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) on the villain phase unless you can dispatch a nasty minion before it gets to activate. (Or have to exhaust with no readies in hand.)

- Solid form + [Deft Focus](/card/16024) + [Martial Prowess](/card/10018) = 5 effective resources set up to generate 3 resources toward attacks almost every turn. This is excellent value.

- [Drop Kick](/card/10014) and [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) help prime villains for [Press the Advantage](/card/04043). [Press the Advantage](/card/04043) is one of your best cards, being a cheap way to replenish your hand with more readies/attacks!

- The best way to benefit from 3x [Fluid Motion](/card/28016) is to play 3 attacks every turn and ready as much as possible. The card draw from [Quick Shift](/card/32040), [Press the Advantage](/card/04043) and [Drop Kick](/card/10014) is essential for fishing for more attacks/readies, allowing you to have HUGE damage turns! 

- Against Stalwart or Steady, you should bring [Colossus](/card/32048) instead of [Mockingbird](/card/01083)

- [Battle Fury](/card/06018) and [Energy](/card/01088) are both great cards you could consider adding. The former is especially useful against minion-heavy scenarios. 
 - The reason Energy is not already included is due to Shadowcat's low cost curve - 23 of her cards are 0-1 cost when including the discount from [Deft Focus](/card/16024), and even more when you factor in Solid form and [Martial Prowess](/card/10018). Quite often, you won't need to spend more than one resource from your hand to play a card. Ideal turns consist of playing your three cheapest attacks, then readying as much as possible!

<hr>
**Good luck, have fun! :D **
<hr>

decklists.name: Float Like a Butterfly, Sting Like a Bee
decklists.description_md: Note: I spent *three hours* working on the original write-up for this deck, and the website ate it (despite saving at multiple stages). Then it refused to let me try again for several days. If something is missing, please let me know, but pls be gentle. It's been a long weekend :'( EDIT: first mistake, [Lie in Wait](/card/13017) is supposed to be [Battle Fury](/card/06018) ![shadowcat](https://external-content.duckduckgo.com/iu/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fstatic0.cbrimages.com%2Fwordpress%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2019%2F11%2FKitty-Pryde-Featured.jpg&f=1&nofb=1&ipt=f827fb79dcdaafb9edb392af5262e683d053ea6834e671c939f9d042c332366e&ipo=images) This [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) deck is primarily focused on defeating enemies while laughing at their attempts to hit you. You are a bit of a glass cannon if enemies manage to land any blows, however. Keep up the pace of the fight and duck into [Phased](/card/32031b) as much as possible to avoid them and hit back with massive damage. **Roll With the Punches** The first thing about [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) is that playing her revolves around getting the most out of [Solid](/card/32031a) / [Phased](/card/32031b). It's subtlely different from other form changers like [Ant-Man](/card/12001a), [Wasp](/card/13001a), and even her closest anologue, [Vision](/card/26001a). Although understanding the card itself isn't all that difficult, there are some non-obvious implications: - [Solid](/card/32031a)'s flip response is not forced, so it is *always optional*. - [Phased](/card/32031b)'s flip response _is_ forced, so it is *always mandatory*. - Shadowcat's mass form upgrade can flip an unlimited number of times per round. - Playing [Quick Shift](/card/32040) *always* counts as defending since you can only play it during an attack. This also always makes you the defender of that attack, whether your used your basic action to defend or not. - [Toe to Toe](/card/32046) has two opportunities to flip your mass form upgrade, first from the villain's attack, and second from the attack on the card itself. - [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) can be used any time you flip your mass form upgrade, even during the villain phase, and [Solid](/card/32031a) can pay for it (if it's ready) after flipping from [Phased](/card/32031b). - [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) similarly allows Shadowcat to ready after flipping her mass form upgrade, even during the villain phase, and even in the middle of resolving other triggers (like [Toe to Toe](/card/32046). **Blow-By-Blow** The main strategy with this deck is to try to stay in [Solid](/card/32031a) as much as possible throughout the player phase and end with your final Attack/Defense in [Phased](/card/32031b). There are some exceptions, like bypassing Guard enemies, where you will want to flip multiple times in the player phase. Others will be elaborated below. *Toe to Toe Combo* [Toe to Toe](/card/32046) does great damage for a relatively low resource cost, but usually you have to pay a larger health cost. Shadowcat circumvents that by preventing all damage with [Phased](/card/32031b). It is ideal to use this while in Phased to start. Here's the sequence: - Play an attack event if in [Solid](/card/32031a) form - Play [Toe to Toe](/card/32046) while in [Phased](/card/32031b) - Defend the villain's attack and take no damage (even better when you can use [Quick Shift](/card/32040) since you won't have to exhaust, plus you'll draw 2 extra cards) - Form upgrade flips to [Solid](/card/32031a) - [Toe to Toe](/card/32046)'s attack resolves, then you can optionally flip back to [Phased](/card/32031b) [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) triggering mid-activation is important here if you don't want to optionally flip back to [Phased](/card/32031b) yet but do want the ready so you can perform another basic action. It can be used from Solid though, if the villain stunned, [Lockheed](/card/32032) is ready to chump block for you, or you have [Quick Shift](/card/32040). The sequence changes slightly: - Play [Toe to Toe](/card/32046) from [Solid](/card/32031a) - Chump block, use the stun, just facetank the damage, or ideally [Quick Shift](/card/32040) immediately to [Phased](/card/32031b) - If you played [Quick Shift](/card/32040), you'll flip back to [Solid](/card/32031a) immediately - Toe to Toe's attack triggers, and your mass form upgrade can optionally flip back to [Phased](/card/32031b) *Surprise Attack Combo* [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) is wonderful in this deck for allowing you stay in [Phased](/card/32031b) as long as possible. Its best use is during the villain phase, but you can definitely do some solid work with it during the player phase as well. Here's the main sequence: - Flip from [Phased](/card/32031b) after attacking or defending - Exhaust [Solid](/card/32031a) to pay for [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) - Flip back to [Phased](/card/32031b) Simple, but there are some fun combos during the villain phase. - Flip from [Phased](/card/32031b) after defending and taking no damage - Exhaust [Solid](/card/32031a) to pay for [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) to hopefully defeat a minion that would otherwise attack - Discard [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) to ready yourself - Flip back to [Phased](/card/32031b) to defend against yet another attack **Expert Pugilist** One of the best combos with this deck is how it all interacts with ATK boosts from [Combat Training](/card/01057) and [Fluid Motion](/card/28016) and readying effects from [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037), [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051), and [Battle Fury](/card/06018). One important thing to keep in mind is that, although Ready to Rumble is limit 1 in play, you can discard it to ready and play another one (and again, if you have all 3) in the same turn, so long as you flip your mass form upgrade, which you can do if you just keep making basic attacks. [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) is particularly useful here because it helps trigger [Fluid Motion](/card/28016)'s ATK boost while also providing a ready to help you immediately capitalise on it. There are plenty of attack events in the deck: [Phase Strike](/card/32038), [Press the Advantage](/card/04043), [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037), [Surprise Attack](/card/13014), and [Toe to Toe](/card/32046). [Press the Advantage](/card/04043) additionally combos with [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) to help accelerate your card draw. It's also a cheap event (that doesn't involve the villain attacking you) if you just want to flip your mass form upgrade and/or trigger [Fluid Motion](/card/28016). **Stamina Training** This deck is notable in that it doesn't include the basic double resources or actually any resources at all. There are only 12 cards in the deck that cost 2 or more resources, and many of them can utilise the deck's many resource generators, often using 1 or fewer cards from hand. As mentioned, there are a few resource generators to help keep the engine running smoothly. There's extra card from [Assess the Situation](/card/12033), [Press the Advantage](/card/04043), [Hall of Heroes](/card/06017), and [Kitty's Room](/card/32033). [Assess the Situation](/card/12033) is also a resource, either right now or an extra card next round. Always save it to spend last, but definitely spend it if you can. It's not worth it to hold back just to draw an extra card if it means you aren't playing a card this round, but it definitely helps smooth out resources with awkward hands where you would otherwise end with additional cards. It's generally a good idea to use [Hall of Heroes](/card/06017) at 6+ counters so that you can flip, draw 3, then draw 3 more on the next round before flipping back up, but since just over half the deck (21 cards) is events, plus the 2 copies of [Phased and Confused](/card/32036), you won't always have much to do with your extra cards, so just flip whenever you can. You can still accelerate some extra card draw with [Kitty's Room](/card/32033). There are a few resource-specific generators or cost-reducers. [The X-Jet](/card/32020), [Deft Focus](/card/16024), [Martial Prowess](/card/10018), and [Solid](/card/32031a). The X-Jet is valuable in that it can be shared with any X-Men hero. In multiplayer, coordinate with your group about who should take it if there are multiple X-Men heroes at the table. [Deft Focus](/card/16024) gets a lot of return on investment, allowing itself to trigger on many of [Shadowcat](/card/32030a)'s cards, so many in fact it's faster to list which cards don't work with it ([Lockheed](/card/32032), [Quick Shift](/card/32040) since it's 0-cost anyway, [Kitty's Room](/card/32033), and [Phased and Confused](/card/32036)). That means it works with literally everything else; all other events: [Airwalk](/card/32039), [Phase Strike](/card/32038), [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037), and other upgrades: [Acute Control](/card/32034) and [Intangible Interference](/card/32035). [Martial Prowess](/card/10018) will help pay for a second attack event per round to keep [Fluid Motion](/card/28016) at maximum. And finally, [Solid](/card/32031a) is very... solid. It provides a for any Attack or Defense event. Although there are no relevant Defense events, there's 14 Attack events here. Additionally, [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) will always get the bonus damage when using [Martial Prowess](/card/10018) or [Solid](/card/32031a) to pay for it. There are a few other surprise efficiency cards in [Acute Control](/card/32034), [Intangible Interference](/card/32035), and [Marked](/card/33032), although the former are a bit scenario-dependent. That said, [Deft Focus](/card/16024) can easily play them onto the board to get them out of your deck if you have nothing better to do with your hand or in early setup. [Acute Control](/card/32034) is often a bit superfluous, since ignoring is enough for most side schemes, but in multiplayer, you can still help your team clear them so others can thwart the main, while also thwarting the main scheme. [Intangible Interference](/card/32035) is less consistent, as not every scenario has Guard minions. Thankfully [Hellfire Pawns](/card/32058) can help you get value out of this if you ever draw [Shadow of the Past](/card/01190). And finally, [Marked](/card/33032) allows any attack, whether it is a basic attack or from an event to have Overkill. Additionally, it's not always necessary since you can ignore Guard minions, but it helps squeeze all of the damage out of every attack. Most of your Attack events are lower to moderate damage, and [Toe to Toe](/card/32046) only targets the villain anyway, but Kitty's ATK can boost quite high. **Back Up Plan** This deck has the capacity to completely invalidate a lot of damage. However, you might get overrun with minions, and thankfully there are some solid tools. As mention previously, [Surprise Attack](/card/13014) can help keep [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) in [Phased](/card/32031b) during the villain phase and also defeat minions before they can activate. In general, the deck is efficient at clearing minions from the board, which will account for most of the damage anyway. In the event of an unlucky [Assault](/card/01187) or something similar, you have [Kitty's Room](/card/32033) to help you heal. Although [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) cannot trigger in Alter-Ego (even if you use your Alter-Ego power to flip her mass form upgrade), it can aid in keeping tempo after healing before flipping back to Hero form later in the same turn. **Southpaw Form** There are quite a few flexible slots in the deck. If you feel like you won't get value out of [Press the Advantage](/card/04043), [Get Over Here!](/card/06014) is a good alternative that costs even less but requires a minion in play. [Clobber](/card/18012) is also a solid Attack event that can be played multiple times per round if you have no other such events in your hand. These options are especially relevant against [Sabretooth I](/card/32060), who heals every time you use [Toe to Toe](/card/32046), drastically lowering its value. Since [Marked](/card/33032) is mainly for getting the most out of your basic attacks, you could opt instead to use [Hand Cannon](/card/16046). It's more expensive, but it can be played whenever you have it, not just when there's a targetable minion, and can additionally boost your ATK even further. This deck excels in multiplayer but can function solo and can cover some threat with cards like [Lockheed](/card/32032), [Airwalk](/card/32039), [Acute Control](/card/32034), [Phased and Confused](/card/32036), and her own basic THW. However, an easy fix to help her handle more threat would be to simply add [Smash the Problem](/card/25019) which will combo well with her up-to-5 ATK. Alternatively, [Chase Them Down](/card/01052) and [Looking for Trouble](/card/16043) will both go a long way to themselves triggering often, helping to trigger other cards, and of course add some extra thwarting.

decklists.name: Stick-Through-It
decklists.description_md:
![](https://i.imgur.com/D5QNoeM.png)

# Why this deck?

A year ago, I made a Shadowcat Pool deck called Intangible Blackout. It revolved around using Kitty's Phased form to mitigate the riskier elements of 'Pool. It was a cool idea, but admittedly it was not the best execution. I published it when 'Pool was still new, and I was not as experienced in building decks. So I decided to take another crack at it, and I ended up with a much stronger deck!

# Live a Little!

This deck is built around playing **[Live Dangerously](/card/44024)**, and KEEPING it in play! When testing verses expert Klaw, I played it turn 1 and easily kept it in play all game, along with the **[Symbiote Suit](/card/27191)** without any issues! This card powers the rest of the deck. It unlocks the full power of **["I Got This"](/card/44021)** and makes it one of the highest value cards in the game. It also fully charges the **[Laser Swords](/card/44055)**, which can be used with all of the readying cards in the deck to slice clean through villains. In solo, the threat is actually quite manageable...though it can be a bit dangerous at times. (But hey, that's the point, right?) In multiplayer, threat is harder to clear, but the benefits are greater. All players draw 2 extra cards, and the acceleration and hazard icons feel less impactful.

# Threat management

In solo, the threat isn't too hard to keep down, even with crisis icons out. While in Phased form, you ignore crisis. So early game, you will be using your basic thwart on the main scheme a lot. **["I Got This"](/card/44021)** is also fantastic for clearing threat through crisis. Since it isn't an attack or thwart, you can use it while stunned/confused, and it won't take you out of phased. Use your extra readying from **[Utopia](/card/33020)**, **[Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037)**, and **[Stick-To-Itiveness](/card/44030)** to remove more threat if needed. Doing this for your last activation will also let you end in phased form, so that you are safe to block in the villain phase. Your allies won't be able to bypass crisis, so they can be used instead to attack or clear any side schemes you don't want out.

**[Distraction](/card/44054)** is a very cheap and easy way to shut off minions. Unfortunately it doesn't work on elites, otherwise it would be a perfect answer to **[Dreadpool](/card/44038)**!

# Card Swaps and Multiplayer Considerations

You may want to throw **[Gambit](/card/48021)** in here. In my testing, he kept wiffing and only pulling 1 boost cards. So for punishment, he is going back into the box. I also had **[Synch](/card/47018)** and **[Stepford Cuckoos](/card/45049)** in the early version of this deck. **[Synch](/card/47018)** can buff Shadowcats thwart, which is great while she's in Phased form. She just felt too expensive just for that purpose. The Cuckoos can get rid of treacheries- which we don't like, and hopefully let you draw minions and side schemes- which this deck can handle very well (or just straight up ignore). Again, it just didn't make the final cut. Shadowcat loves **[Barely a Scratch](/card/44017)**, as it lets her block all damage in phased form without exhausting. I didn't find it necessary here at all, but try it if you'd like. **[Specialized Training](/card/43021)** is very hard to clear in solo, and its especially tough if you already have **[Live Dangerously](/card/44024)** out and don't want to remove it. The benefit you would get from the extra +1 thwart is very high, but in solo you may want to swap it with something else, like another ally.

Adjust the resources to your preference. If you aren't a big fan of the 'Pool resources, swap them for their basic counterparts. I've found that I can usually keep my health high enough for them to at least count as doubles, but in rare cases they end up as single resources when your health is low.

I did most of the testing in solo, but I did some 2 player as well. I think 2 player is about the limit for managing threat without some help. Higher player counts would require coordination. A justice player that can play **[Heroic Intuition](/card/01065)** on Shadowcat and some **[Crisis Averted](/card/15012)** would really help!

I just had to sneak one more Utopia deck in there before we moved on to S.H.I.E.L.D. stuff! xD Let me know what you think about it in the comments!

decklists.name: Kitty Hits the Griddy 2: Electric Boogaloo
decklists.description_md:
Shadowcat can guarantee the triggers on **[Unflappable](/card/09020)** and **[Hard to Ignore](/card/16017)** using her **[Phased](/card/32031b)** constant effect, with minimal investment and often ending up with more cards in hand. With her defense well covered from her kit alone and extra resources from [Quick Shift](/card/32040) and [Unflappable](/card/09020) to prepare **tech**; we look to **[Repurpose](/card/31016)** to provide her with excellent burst thwart and damage. Using some neat cards like **[Jocasta](/card/26013)**, who recurs **[Quick Shift](/card/32040)**, and **[Forcefield Generator](/card/31019)**, which protects against small pings until going out in a blaze of glory, we can control and set up until it's time to burst down the villain. This deck was inspired by my previous deck, **Gwen Hits the Griddy**. Shadowcat and Ghost Spider have some notable differences. Ghost Spider readies easier for [Repurpose](/card/31016), while Shadowcat takes no damage for cheaper. Ghost Spider's damage potential is higher, but Shadowcat's better economy and thwart give her a flexible early game. Ghost Spider runs [True Grit](/card/18031) and Web-Warriors, while Shadowcat can afford and avoid the downsides of [Forcefield Generator](/card/31019).
## **How Does Shadowcat Work** ## Take a look at this video from community member **SC0E** who put out a great video explaining Shadowcat! This is a great primer on all the little quirks she presents. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2431JkwTEqY
## **Basic Form Technique** ## - [Phased](/card/32031b) is a **Forced Response**, making it mandatory to flip after an attack or defense and giving it timing priority over regular **Responses** - [Solid](/card/32031a) is merely a **Response** meaning the flip from [Solid](/card/32031a) to [Phased](/card/32031b) is optional after attacking or defending - **Attack** and **Defense** cards count as attacking and defending for [Phased](/card/32031b) and [Solid](/card/32031a), in addition to basic powers - Basic defending or playing a *(defense)* event only **begins** the defense. The defense shares an end window with the attack, so [Unflappable](/card/09020) and [Solid](/card/32031a)/[Phased](/card/32031b) do not trigger when Shadowcat plays her *(defense)*, but only **after** the defense ends, which is after step 4 of the enemy attack Basically, we want to end every hero phase in [Phased](/card/32031b), by flipping from [Solid](/card/32031a) with our last attack of the turn (remember we don't have to flip after every attack since [Solid](/card/32031a) is optional). Then we want to defend the villain attack, guaranteeing we take no damage.
## **Intermediate Form Stances** ## - When an enemy attack begins we can use [Quick Shift](/card/32040). As an **Interrupt**, it immediately draw 2 cards, before the attack resolves. As a *(defense)* card, this makes the attack considered defended without needing to exhaust - [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) is essentially [Indomitable](/card/01082) for any aspect. If we exhausted to defend and thus trigger the **Forced Response** on [Phased](/card/32031b) to form change, we can trigger [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) to ready. This is useful if we need to defend again or to start the hero phase unexhausted, guaranteeing an attack that can return Shadowcat to [Phased](/card/32031b) - [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) can trigger after we defend and use the **Forced Response** on [Phased](/card/32031b). Since it is an attack, it gives us the option to flip back to [Phased](/card/32031b). Useful if we need to defend again, or the first thing we want to do in the hero phase requires being phased such as *Selective Intangibility*, [Airwalk](/card/32039), [Phase Strike](/card/32038) - After the defense finishes, we will draw 1 card from [Unflappable](/card/09020), remove 1 threat from the main scheme with [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017), and deal 1 damage to the attacker with [Electrostatic Armor](/card/10031) This is the baseline, and it's already very good. Now let's turn it up a couple notches.
## **Advanced Form Mastery** ## Very important is that [Phased](/card/32031b) is a **Forced Response**, so the flip to [Solid](/card/32031a) occurs before all of our "after defends" **Response** cards such as [Unflappable](/card/09020), [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017), [Electrostatic Armor](/card/10031), [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022), and [Counter-Punch](/card/01077). The order the **Response** effects trigger is interchangeable. Rarely it matters, but remember that these can be triggered in the order of your choosing for when it does. More on this later. We could not play a [Quick Shift](/card/32040) drawn off of [Unflappable](/card/09020) here, since [Quick Shift](/card/32040)'s **Interrupt** timing is at the start of the attack; but we could play [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) drawn off [Unflappable](/card/09020), triggering a form change). - If we start in [Phased](/card/32031b), defend to flip to [Solid](/card/32031a), then [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) to flip back to [Phased](/card/32031b), our [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017) trigger will benefit from our ability to ignore **crisis**, since we are still in the same response window of "after you defended and took no damage". This would not work if Shadowcat ended in [Solid](/card/32031a), and is one example for the order of the triggers mattering - If we draw a second [Quick Shift](/card/32040) off the first, it is immediately playable, allowing us to draw 4 cards. [Quick Shift](/card/32040) can also draw into [Counter-Punch](/card/01077), which will be relevant later - In multiplayer, [Quick Shift](/card/32040) can make Shadowcat the new target of an attack since it is playable on an attack made against any player and *(defense)* makes her the defender. For example, in 2-player, Shadowcat basic defends the first attack from [Phased](/card/32031b), [Unflappable](/card/09020) draws [Counter-Punch](/card/01077), [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) puts [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) back in [Phased](/card/32031b), [Quick Shift](/card/32040) pulls the second attack, fully resolving in [Phased](/card/32031b) amounting to two attacks with no damage taken. [Shadow and Steel](/card/32050) also draws attacks against any player and works best from [Solid](/card/32031a), saving a [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022) or [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) and being paid for with [Solid](/card/32031a)'s free resource
Benefits so far: - Have mitigated step 1 villain phase threat with [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017) - Have mitigated step 2 of the villain phase by taking no damage from 1-2 villain attacks with [Phased](/card/32031b) - Have an effective 6 card hand with [Unflappable](/card/09020), and sometimes 7-8 card hand with 1-2 [Quick Shift](/card/32040) - Have potentially dealt villain/minion damage with [Counter-Punch](/card/01077), [Electrostatic Armor](/card/10031), or [Shadow and Steel](/card/32050) Since we have effectively turned off the villain for most of the villain phase with little effort, we really only need to answer encounter cards and beat the villain. My answer is [Repurpose](/card/31016). Increasing ATK takes care of minions and the villain, increasing THW takes care of side schemes, and the ready is good security against exhaustion/status and makes sure we can always get to [Phased](/card/32031b).
## **Tech Picks** ## Similar to my previous deck, **Gwen Hits the Griddy**, rather than double down on our defensive efforts, we will be looking for ways to turn our defense into offense. This is primarily for 1-2 player counts, where being well-rounded is better than being laser-focused. - **[Repurpose](/card/31016)** is a great way to supplement the offense of heroes with good access to readies - **[Electrostatic Armor](/card/10031)** is our main tech choice. It already flows well with our 1-2 defenses per round and is cheap. We are running two because this will be our primary [Repurpose](/card/31016) target- - **[Plasma Pistol](/card/20022)** makes the cut over [Energy Barrier](/card/05017) in our 2-cost spot. Shadowcat takes damage so irregularly, that getting the pings from [Energy Barrier](/card/05017) is inconsistent. [Plasma Pistol](/card/20022) is useful to tee up minions to the right health or ping toughs to let our large attacks thru - **[Forcefield Generator](/card/31019)** is a great one-of. Because of how little damage we take, it can stick around for awhile without discarding itself from its **Forced Interrupt**. Being max 1 and having good longevity means we really only want one copy, but it can stick around for a mega turn! - With [Repurpose](/card/31016), [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037), [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022), and [Professor X](/card/32019), we have 10 readies in deck to make use of these boosted stats. **[Ready to Rumble](/card/21022)** is showing that it is more flexible than [Indomitable](/card/01082) here, since we can trigger it in the hero phase after attacking and triggering a form change). The sequence would be [Repurpose](/card/31016)->attack->form change->ready to rumble->attack. At any point we are in [Solid](/card/32031a), we can play [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) using [Solid](/card/32031a)'s resource and [Deft Focus](/card/16024) to deal 3 damage and attack again! - Remember when we said we would come back to drawing into **[Counter-Punch](/card/01077)** off of [Quick Shift](/card/32040)/[Unflappable](/card/09020)? When we [Repurpose](/card/31016) for attack in the hero phase, and then defend in the villain phase, we can trigger [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) to deal our boosted ATK value! This works because [Repurpose](/card/31016) boosts last until the *end of the round*, and as established earlier, the response window stays open throughout all of our "after defends" **Response** effects. This boosted [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) can be played off of any of the numerous defenses Shadowcat will make or as a card drawn by [Quick Shift](/card/32040)/[Unflappable](/card/09020). I've played some 7 ATK [Counter-Punch](/card/01077)s with this deck, but presumably it can get as high as 9! - Thwarting sequencing is a little more restricted, since we still need to attack at least once to get back to [Phased](/card/32031b). [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022) is tougher to pull off since a basic THW won't trigger a form change. But when Shadowcat does boost, ignoring **crisis** while [Phased](/card/32031b) can be beneficial to maximize value with fewer readies - **[Professor X](/card/32019)** is useful as a confuse+3 THW that isn't tied to stopping an attack like [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) is. The 3 THW means we can more often use [Repurpose](/card/31016) to boost attack, and his built in ready effect can let us swing again. We aren't running [Utopia](/card/33020) because triggering the ready effect is less reliable as [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) doesn't need allies, much like [Ghost-Spider](/card/27001a)
## **Superpowers** ## - **[Deft Focus](/card/16024)** hits [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037), [Phase Strike](/card/32038), [Airwalk](/card/32039), [Acute Control](/card/32034), and [Intangible Interference](/card/32035) - **[Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037)** is our best card after [Quick Shift](/card/32040), at base 3 damage, 2 thwart, and a flip to [Phased](/card/32031b); but the numbers only go up with [Repurpose](/card/31016). [Solid](/card/32031a)+[Deft Focus](/card/16024) combine for a lot of free [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037)s - Note that [Solid](/card/32031a) with **[Phase Strike](/card/32038)** is less good, since [Phase Strike](/card/32038) resolves before [Solid](/card/32031a)'s **Response** can flip her to [Phased](/card/32031b), meaning she won't be able to discard an attachment. [Deft Focus](/card/16024) takes the place of [Solid](/card/32031a) here - **[Airwalk](/card/32039)** is amazing when paid for free from [Phased](/card/32031b), but don't overlook the option to play it for a base 2 threat removal as well - **[Intangible Interference](/card/32035)** can be great when we have a boosted thwart stat from [Repurpose](/card/31016) or can play a full strength [Airwalk](/card/32039). It gives a bonus 2 threat removal from a **crisis** side scheme at the cost of an exhaust, useful for things like [Hydra Patrol](/card/04154) or [Abduction Protocols](/card/32100). This must be done from [Phased](/card/32031b) - **[Acute Control](/card/32034)** is a bit more situational. Ignoring **guard** requires an attack from [Phased](/card/32031b) and thus a forced flip to [Solid](/card/32031a). While it can be useful against [Goblin Thrall](/card/02024)s, [M-Type Sentinel](/card/32146)s, and [Master Mold II](/card/32110), Shadowcat will still need a second attack to get back to [Phased](/card/32031b). Both of the upgrades are great [Caught Off Guard](/card/01188) fodder. Thinning the deck, perfect when there's an extra Deft Focus lying around
## **Notables** ## - **[Jocasta](/card/26013)** probably deserves her own section. She gets us a 3rd use of our best card, [Quick Shift](/card/32040), turning her into 2 ER for 4 THW and a block, or 2 ER for 2 THW and 2 blocks. Insane value. Getting 3-4 free blocks per deck cycle allows us to save our exhausts for big [Repurpose](/card/31016) turns - **[The X-Jet](/card/32020)** is a good economy card for the things [Deft Focus](/card/16024) can't touch, like the tech cards and allies. **[Honorary X-Men](/card/33035)** is here to give [Kitty Pride](/card/32030b) the **X-Men** trait so she can benefit from the in alter-ego. Useful to clear a few cards that give us a hard time like [Frozen](/card/21158) and [Seduced](/card/21179). The +1 hit point is situationally useful, against Ebony Maw’s spells for instance - **[Phased and Confused](/card/32036)** can sometimes be a hindrance since we can't trigger [Unflappable](/card/09020) if the villain doesn't attack. Turning off a villain attack and then drawing into [Quick Shift](/card/32040) feels really bad. It’s expensive and doesn’t working with [Deft Focus](/card/16024) or [Solid](/card/32031a). The confuse is useful, but against non-steady villains, [Professor X](/card/32019) is a better confuse. [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) can be good in circumstances where Shadowcat is stuck in [Solid](/card/32031a) or if she can hit [Unflappable](/card/09020) by defending a minion instead. It can buy time early game, before our [Unflappable](/card/09020) engine is set up. Just be careful when playing it that it doesn't shut down the engine entirely! - **[Kitty's Room](/card/32033)** is amazing burst heal. With two uses and a REC, mitigated by our copious readies, she can heal 7 damage quickly. Shadowcat *can* take no damage over the course of the game, but using her health as a resource can generate a lot of tempo in certain situations. Having the option to heal quickly comes in handy. When combined with *Phase Control*, she can choose the healing or draw depending on what's useful or what is in hand. If we have [Phase Strike](/card/32038) and the villain has an attachment, rolling into [Phased](/card/32031b) is prudent. If we just REC and have [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037), roll up to [Solid](/card/32031a) to pay for it and ready. If we have no way to attack, roll up to [Phased](/card/32031b) to prepare for the villain phase - In multiplayer with my Colossus deck, I replace x1 [Plasma Pistol](/card/20022) with x1 **[Shadow and Steel](/card/32021)**. It can draw attacks from other players, trigger [Unflappable](/card/09020), and deal some damage to the villain or hopefully clear a minion. This helps preserve Colossus' toughs ## **Should We Only Defend From Phased?** ## The benefits of defending from [Phased](/card/32031b) are clear: 1. Take no damage 2. Draw 2 cards from [Quick Shift](/card/32040) 3. Trigger [Unflappable](/card/09020) and [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017) If Shadowcat cannot meet these criteria, then she should not defend. She typically only wants to flip to [Phased](/card/32031b) off of [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) or after spending the [Solid](/card/32031a) in the hero phase; rather than flipping to [Phased](/card/32031b) from a defense trigger. Having reliable access to starting in [Phased](/card/32031b) and using [Quick Shift](/card/32040) three times per deck cycle (with help from [Jocasta](/card/26013)), should keep us covered; but what should Shadowcat do when attacked while in [Solid](/card/32031a), such as after a first defense from [Phased](/card/32031b) or the rare occasion of starting a villain phase in [Solid](/card/32031a)? My baseline advice is don't defend in [Solid](/card/32031a), unless able to meet 1., 2., or 3. above. Blocking some damage is not worth the expenditure in exhausts or resources. There are a handful allies that can stick around as emergency chumps, but don’t be afraid to tank a full attack. [Kitty's Room](/card/32033) can burst heal [Kitty Pride](/card/32030b), so taking damage is a minor inconvenience. However, if we can guarantee a combination of the above points, defending from [Solid](/card/32031a) becomes a better value proposition. - [Quick Shift](/card/32040) can get us 1. and 3. for instance, by flipping to [Phased](/card/32031b) and thus taking no damage. Though losing the draw 2 is a shame. Definitely evaluate if it is worth it to burn a [Quick Shift](/card/32040) this way before playing it, as holding it for next turn to defend and draw 2 is also viable - Defending a minion attack or having [Forcefield Generator](/card/31019) active can guarantee 1. And 3, while also saving some energy counters - Multiplayer provides more reason to defend from [Solid](/card/32031a). [Shadow and Steel](/card/32021) can use the [Solid](/card/32031a) resource, hitting 1. and 3. We can use [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) after our first defense from [Phased](/card/32031b) to flip back and take a second attack from [Phased](/card/32031b). Lastly, we can exhaust to defend in [Solid](/card/32031a) as long as we have an in-hand [Quick Shift](/card/32040) for the second defense from [Phased](/card/32031b)

decklists.description_md:
Shadowcat is really good at sneak attacking and phasing to not take damage. This appearing, doing damage, and disappearing makes her the ninja!

## Surprise Attack
The most powerful aspect of Shadowcat is that she doesn't take damage when defending in [Phased](/card/32031b) mass form. So this deck leans into this as a combo. Defend, flip to [Solid](/card/32031a), use the resource generator in [Solid](/card/32031a) to [Surprise Attack](/card/13014), then flip back to [Phased](/card/32031b).

[Quick Shift](/card/32040) lets you defend without exhausting, so they'll assist in helping you not take damage in Phased form and kicking off that combo to strike and get back to Phased.

[Ready to Rumble](/card/21022) lets you ready back in the combo if you had to defend by exhaustion. Leave it out for such a rainy day!

## Attack Exhausted
Sometimes, you have to exhaust and might get caught in Solid. [Pulse Grenade](/card/17023) is meant to be on the board for just such a moment. Trigger [Pulse Grenade](/card/17023), then flip to Phased for the villain phase.

## Throw/Damage Spread
Any good ninja job has the throw action. [Plan B](/card/27024) and [Jarnbjorn](/card/06019) will help you throw resources and cards to do damage spread. Because of the Defend, Attack, and Flip combo, you may end up with an odd mix of cards on the hero phase or a [Ready to Rumble](/card/21022) that you can’t play. Throw your cards into damage to keep the deck flowing. Both [Plan B](/card/27024) and [Jarnbjorn](/card/06019) are especially useful because they aren’t attacks. So they can damage without worrying about stuns or guards, adding to the damage spread capabilities

## Hidden Ninja Attacks
The second most powerful ability is for Shadowcat to ignore Crisis, Guard, and Patrol. So don't forget that when you attack in Phased form or trigger [Pulse Grenade](/card/17023). Then you can use her [Intangible Interference](/card/32035) and [Acute Control](/card/32034) to do extra thwarting and damage. [Looking for Trouble](/card/16043) is great for ignoring Crisis, allowing [Intangible Interference](/card/32035) to activate, giving thwart spread. And friendly reminder that [Looking for Trouble](/card/16043) bypasses **When Revealed** effects because it puts the minion into play.

## Interceptor
Sometimes, you need to your faithful companion to come in, do some damage, and take a hit. [Lockheed](/card/32032) is perfect for this. He can come in, do damage or thwart, and defend for Shadowcat. He'll hopefully always come in at the right time, like an interceptor.

Shadowcat can sneak in the shadows, attack quickly, and sneak back before the villain can hit her. She's absolutely the ninja.

decklists.name: Shadowcat Can Dance All Day
decklists.description_md:
**A.B.D. Always Be Defending.**

This deck is designed for a 4-player X-Men team.

Shadowcat is here to take the heat off her teammates while they stay in hero form. The primary strategy is to intercept attacks, negate the damage with Phased or Tough, and then ready up to defend again.

### Updates
* +1 Shadow and Steel (combo with Colossus teammate)
* -1 Side Step

### Defense events
* Counter-Punch - Shadowcat staple. Allows Shadowcat to flip back over to Phased.
* Never Back Down - Protect your team by stunning the enemy. Easy to achieve the condition using Phased/Tough.
* Perseverance - Use when forced to flip into Solid to stay safe.
* Powerful Punch - Another staple. Counts as both an Attack and Defense for phasing shenanigans.
* Preemptive Strike - Primarily here for the "defense" tag. Allows Shadowcat to intercept attacks without using her basic activation.
* Side Step - Prevent 3 damage for cheap. Optional.

### Allies
This deck revolves around having a hand full of defense events, so allies are kept at a minimum.

### Resources
The mana curve is pretty low, so doubles have been omitted. Defense Energy is included because it will always always be possible to get free value from it.

### Supports
All of the key X-Men support cards have been given to her teammates. Kitty doesn't mind; she just wants to keep drawing defense events.

### Upgrades
Electrostatic Armor is here for a little bit of ping damage, which may help knock off Tough statuses and kill chump minions. Ready to Rumble allows us to intercept attacks for multiple teammates in the same round.

### Notable omissions
Similar decks run Defiance, Deft Focus, Flow LIke Water, and Hard to Ignore. Simply put, I don't have a complete collection. Feel free to swap these in according to taste.

### Additional notes
This deck is specifically created for a team that includes Colossus. If not playing with him, swap out Shadow and Steel.

### Credits
This deck is heavily inspired by decks like dr00's Drunken Master and VillainTheory's Nine Lives.

decklists.name: Chump Blocking is Sooooooooooo 2024.
decklists.description_md:
Nothing earth shattering here. It's a deck that's filled with x-men allies, resource generators, and utopia. Maybe a bit "samey" but keeping Shadowcat in phased form has never been easier. The number one priority is obviously Utopia. There are 3 ways to get it on the first turn (Forge, Build Support, and the card itself). Mulligan hard to get this card. There's a roughly 2/3 chance that with a mulligan you'll end up with one of the 3 cards needed to get utopia out. If not, play an ally or two just to take care of the board while you block for everyone.  

Once it's out, there's a simple pattern of block, play an ally, attack to change form and let your allies do the rest. The flexibility of the allies in play allows you to easily control the board. Not only is it an incredibly strong deck, but it's also incredibly fun. Let Shadowcat do her thing and let the allies do the rest. 

Notes: Endurance is included as a backup on the off chance she has to take a hit. Face the Past also provides a nice ready and card draw. While her nemesis minion causes a confuse, in my play experience, used when there are an ally or two on the table usually just allows for card draw and a form switch. Switching these out for an ally will provide slightly improved odds for finding an ally, although in my experience, this hasn't really been an issue. 

This deck has been used to take down Venom Goblin in solo expert and expert campaign mode with the symbiote suit.

decklists.name: The Power of Shadowcat (Justice)
decklists.description_md:
In this deck, Shadowcat shows off the Power of Justice (specifically mutant Justice / Peackeeping)!

Kitty is recruiting X-men allies and other mutant(s) like [Jessica Jones](/card/01059) and helping them bypass crisis icons using her [Phased](/card/32031b) mass form and [Mutant Peacekeepers](/card/34018)...

The main combo of this deck uses 4 pieces:

• Get [Jessica Jones](/card/01059) onto the board and place an [Honorary X-Men](/card/33035) onto her.

• Use [One Way or Another](/card/22015) to grab out side schemes (ideally with acceleration or crisis icons) on them - this will boost Jessica's THW

• Use [Mutant Peacekeepers](/card/34018) to exhaust Shadowcat and Jessica and constantly deplete the main scheme

You'll likely get other X-men down along the way and even place [Mission Training](/card/34016) onto them but keeping 8-9 THW handy via [Mutant Peacekeepers](/card/34018) is key. Because you can spread the thwart removal you can keep the side schemes at low threat and pick them off when essential or leave them out to pump up your thwart potential.

You can afford to leave your allies on the board because of Shadowcats extreme ability to avoid damage. 

• Begin the villain phase in [Phased](/card/32031b) and defend (either naturally or with [Quick Shift](/card/32040)- this will flip you to [Solid](/card/32031a).

• On your turn play a [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) to deal some damage and ready your hero. This will flip you back to [Phased](/card/32031b).

• Luckily your massform abilities don't trigger from thwart actions - so finish up your turn with a big [Mutant Peacekeepers](/card/34018) play. As more X-men Justice allies come out this deck is sure to change. 

The largest I've gotten [Mutant Peacekeepers](/card/34018) was 15 - let me know if you get higher with some risk-reward [Jessica Jones](/card/01059) play!

• Shadowcat Base [2] + Heroic Intuition [1] + Jessica Jones [6] + Blindfold with Mission Training [3] + Banshee with Mission Training [3].

Have fun out there enjoying the Power of Shadowcat in Justice! If you like this deck be sure to give it a ♥ and check out the Power of Shadowcat Episode by Marvel Champions Monthly Podcast!

https://mcm-podcast.com/2022/10/09/mcm-76-power-of-shadowcat-feat-andy-n/

decklists.name: Shadowcat- Rogue n' Ready
decklists.description_md:
[Shadowcat](https://marvelcdb.com/card/32030a) is my favorite character in Marvel Champions, but I've never really built a deck for her.  There are so many good decks out there for her, with [dr00](https://marvelcdb.com/user/profile/5/dr00)'s ["Drunken Master"](https://marvelcdb.com/decklist/view/23166/drunken-master-1.0) deck being my absolute favorite to play. You will still see some of the bones of that deck here!

I initially started thinking of modifying the deck with [Ready for a Fight](https://marvelcdb.com/card/52019), which could help with those odd times where I could not get back to phased form. Then, I saw [Boomguy](https://marvelcdb.com/user/profile/6643/boomguy)'s [Rogue](https://marvelcdb.com/card/48012) challenge, and thought this would be the perfect opportunity to try something a little different with Kitty.

The idea behind this deck is for Kitty to defend and not take any damage, leaving her plenty of heath to fuel Rogue's ability. Energy Barrier and Med Team will keep Rogue safe from perishing due to consequential damage. The 7 cards that provide readying for Shadowcat allow her to be a true partner with Rogue rather than just a defender. 

It's not the strongest Shadowcat deck, but I've had a lot of fun with it!  The deck centers around getting Rogue out with an Energy Shield, but Kitty has enough flexibility to handle some turns on her own until Rogue makes her entrance.

Here is a breakdown of the card choices:

**Allies**

Shadowcat doesn't need a ton of allies, but of course [Rogue](https://marvelcdb.com/card/48012) is a must for this deck. [Jocasta](https://marvelcdb.com/card/26013) is great for recurring Quick Strike, one of Kitty's best cards.


**Events**

Shadowcat will be taking most of the hits, so a good number of defense events are necessary to allow Rogue to do Rogue things. These are:

[Defiance](https://marvelcdb.com/card/26018)- a nice affordable defense
[Powerful Punch](https://marvelcdb.com/card/32014)- deals damage and gets her to phased form to take no damage before flipping back to solid. Solid form can also help pay for it.
[Preemptive strike](https://marvelcdb.com/card/05014)- another affordable event that can deal the villain (or the villainous) some damage
[What Doesn't Kill Me](https://marvelcdb.com/card/27016)-- Not a defense event, but since Rogue will be doing Kitty some damage, this will allow her to heal and get a ready out of it. Also, many of Kitty's defense events won't work on minions (since no boost card is turned over), so it will help us there as well. 

**Player Side Scheme**

[Specialized Training](https://marvelcdb.com/card/43021) will optimize Shadowcat Surprise and other readying cards

**Resources**

This deck is built with lots of energy and physical resources to power Energy Shield, WDKM, and RFAF. I left out the double science resource to minimize other resources. Power of Protection helps with some of the pricier protection cards.

**Upgrades and Supports**

Resource Generators: [X-Jet](https://marvelcdb.com/card/32020) is the most important to help generate the resource you need to play some of her cards. [Helicarrier](https://marvelcdb.com/card/01092) helps with economy, [Med Team](https://marvelcdb.com/card/01080) can heal Rogue or Shadowcat. 

[Hard to Ignore](https://marvelcdb.com/card/16017) is a good card to handle extra threat, and it carries physical  resources for WDKM/RFAF.

Two copies of [Energy Shield](https://marvelcdb.com/card/52018) are included because Rogue will need one ASAP.

[Ready for a Fight](https://marvelcdb.com/card/52019) will allow Kitty to safely flip down and get some healing in plus an extra card. Even better, it will allow you to get to Phased form if you got stuck in Solid during the player phase!

Finally, [Ready to Rumble](https://marvelcdb.com/card/21022) provides 2 more readies for Shadowcat. I also realized, while building this deck, that Ready to Rumble can get Kitty readied back up if her nasty obligation forces her to flip from solid to phased while she is exhausted. This can help mitigate one of the most annoying obligations in the game.

decklists.name: Kittypool's Five Finger Discount
decklists.description_md: This deck is built around the idea of reducing the cost to play cards for explosive turns, benefiting from powerful 'Pool aspect cards while minimizing the trade-offs, and a couple readys for good measure. ### Stop paying full cost for cards - All of Kitty's identity specific events are **Superpowers**, so [Deft Focus](/card/16024) and [X-Gene](/card/38019) are the core setup pieces to allow you to play these events for little to no cost. [The X-Jet](/card/32020) gives you yet another generator, and of course, Kitty comes with her own built-in generator when she's in [Solid](/card/32031a) mass form. That's up to four effective resources per turn. - [Deadpool Corps Ship](/card/44049) allows you to play **'Pool** allies without paying their cost. Since they don't take consequential damage, and Kitty can often defend safely from [Phased](/card/32031b) form, it should be relatively easy to keep allies on the board. Although it's better to defend without exhausting in phased form when possible, between allies and events, your basic powers are not the main attraction (most of the time). Regardless, you don't need to chump block as much as some heroes, so you can get a lot of value out of these allies in exchange for a single encounter card. - [Self Confidence](/card/44025), [Self Control](/card/44026), and [Self Preservation](/card/44027) are nice triple energies when you have full health. Speaking of.... ### Mutant Healing - [Healing Factor](/card/44029) provides 2 HP of recovery each turn (and is also a **Superpower**, so can benefit from [Deft Focus](/card/16024)) - [X-Mansion](/card/32049) and [Kitty's Room](/card/32033) can also provide a little additional healing. Since this deck will prefer to spend most of your time in hero form, it helps to make the most out of your time in Alter-Ego. - [Symbiote Suit](/card/27191) gives you an extra 10 HP for survivability, and don't forget your **REC** also counts as a basic power that benefits from the +1. ### Stay ready This deck also has several ways to ready. Even if you do exhaust for a defense or recovery, there is often a way to ready. - The eponymous [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) is an identity-specific event, a superpower, and an attack, meaning that you can discount it with [Deft Focus](/card/16024), [X-Gene](/card/38019), and/or [Solid](/card/32031a) (only two of these are needed since it's a 2 cost card). - The classic [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) is great because it can be triggered either by flipping your identity or your mass form. This is especially nice when you basic defend in Phased form. - The 'Pool aspect also gave us a a cheap ready option in [Stick-To-Itiveness](/card/44030). Unlike cards like Ready to Rumble and Tenacity, this is not discarded giving you a 1-cost ready each round. You can't use Solid as the kicker, but X-Jet will work. - [Professor X](/card/32019) also gives a ready option, along with a 3-threat removal and a chump blocker. ### Basic powers With a 2-2-2 stat line, Shadowcat is already a pretty versatile hero. I already mentioned [Symbiote Suit](/card/27191) which adds 1 to each of those, but if you have [Laser Swords](/card/44055), it sort of adds 2 to your attack (by ensuring there is a **Hazard** icon in play). Once Stick-To-Itiveness is in play, you should aim to defend in every villain phase and use a basic power in every hero phase. ### Hand size and Draw This deck really doesn't have much by way of card draw or tutoring. [Mulligan](/card/44048) can be a good way to work through your deck, and since [Kitty Pride](/card/32030b) can flip her mass form once a turn at will, you'll usually have your choice of drawing or healing from [Kitty's Room](/card/32033). The biggest help in this regard will be the extra card from [Symbiote Suit](/card/27191), along with in-play resource generators so you can play most of your hand each round. Although you always want to end your turn in Hero Phased form, it's especially important if you have [Quick Shift](/card/32040) in hand. This lets you take no damage without needing to exhaust and lets you draw two cards. [Live Dangerously](/card/44024) gives you an extra 2 hand size, at the expense of a bunch of icons. Often, Shadowcat doesn't mind these, however, since she can ignore Crisis, and negate the extra damage from the Amplify icon when defending. It also pumps up her [Laser Swords](/card/44055). Once you've got the Symbiote Suit, that extra hazard icon can be brutal, so I prefer it early game to help get my setup cards out quickly, or late game to go for the kill, and I try not to keep it around too long.

decklists.name: Kittypool: Intangible Blackout
decklists.description_md:
### **Lights Out**


![](https://i.pinimg.com/736x/26/b8/4a/26b84a8538ada13a504631a121065d04.jpg)

Kitty is perfect for the 'Pool aspect. She ignores crisis icons with her [_Selective Intangibility_](/card/32030a) ability, ignores amplify icons with her Phased form, and doesn't need to chump block so she can make full use of the 'Pool allies!

### Strategy:



Stay in hero form, phased defend each turn, while chipping away with your 'Pool allies. Finish off the villain with a pair of hyper powered [Bazookas](/card/44052) to the face!

### The Icons:


**Crisis:** By thwarting in phased form, you can completely ignore this. So stack up all the crisis icons you want, who cares! Keep in mind, your allies won't be able to thwart the main scheme, so have them attack instead.

**Amplify:** Similar to crisis, we don't really mind this one. Just watch out for villainous minions or the potential for multiple activations!

**Acceleration:** Having a few of these out isn't a problem. Especially if you have your upgrades to manage threat on the board ([Blackout](/card/44053), [Intangible Interference](/card/32035), and [Stick-To-Itiveness](/card/44030).)

**Hazard:** This one is definitely the worst. [Symbiote Suit](/card/27191) can be worth playing at the right time for the extra draw and health. Plus getting an extra card from ["I Got This"](/card/44021).

### Staying Alive


Basic Defending is always an option. But if you have [Quick Shift](/card/32040), that's even better, as it lets you defend while keeping your basic activation to thwart. 'Pool introduces another way for her to do this, with [Barely a Scratch](/card/44017). This card is great because you can wait to see how much damage you'll take first before you decide to use it. If you are in solid form this can put you back into phased, ready to defend again or ready to thwart on your turn!

[Healing Factor](/card/44029) is a key card here as we don't want to flip to alter ego, and this will deal with any chip damage you take from minions or extra villain activations.

### Threat Management: 


<s>[Blackout](/card/44053) normally trades 1 threat removed for 1 resource. Nothing too flashy. But with this deck, we can consistently turn this into 3 threat for 1 resource! By combining this card with [Intangible Interference](/card/32035), along with our crisis icon generators ( [Ambush](/card/44051) and [Distraction](/card/44054)), we will have threat handled each turn.</s> (Note:[Intangible Interference](/card/32035) only removes threat from the scheme with a crisis icon, so it can't be used to remove threat from the main) [The X-Jet](/card/32020) gives us an way to trigger this every turn even when we don't have the right resources in hand. Before we have this combo online, [Airwalk](/card/32039), basic thwart with [Stick-To-Itiveness](/card/44030), and ["I Got This"](/card/44021) will have the threat covered.

### Damage:


Our 'Pool allies will be providing consistent damage throughout the game. Shadowcat can ignore guard and patrol, making guard minions low priority targets. [Headpool](/card/44014), [Lockheed](/card/32032), and [Bob, Agent of Hydra](/card/44043) all have ways to sort of get around guard as well. [Kidpool](/card/44015) doesn't, but the piercing is very valuable. Play the [Bazookas](/card/44052) whenever you can, and use them as a finisher after building up icons with 'Pool allies, [Distraction](/card/44054) and [Ambush](/card/44051). [Live Dangerously](/card/44024) is not something you want to have stay on the board. Use it on the final turn to combo with the [Bazookas](/card/44052) or alongside ["I Got This"](/card/44021).


### Final Thoughts:


This deck has a very interesting and unique feel to it that highlights an underutilized part of Kitty's kit. I've taken it against both expert Klaw and expert Project Wideawake. They were great matchups that I highly recommend! Any scenario with a lot of icons (especially crisis), along with guard and patrol minions will make for a good fight. 

If you want to cut that last card or make any swaps, you could try dropping [Get Rage-y](/card/44020). [Ambush](/card/44051) and [Distraction](/card/44054) can be adjusted, depending on the scenario.

This is a solo focused deck, and can seriously mess up multiplayer games with the reliance on crisis icons. I think it could work in a two player game, but keeping the threat down could be tough if they flip to AE a lot. I'd recommend playing with a partner that does not flip a lot, or have them bring ways to confuse the villain.

decklists.name: Shadowcat - Strength in Diversity
decklists.description_md:
My first attempt at a [Shadowcat](/card/32030a)/[Strength in Diversity](/card/53019) build.

Use one deck pass to set up. Prioritize getting your allies on board then Support/Upgrades ([The Triskelion](/card/01073) is the exception, we want this out asap). Once we get the Triskelion out, our fourth slot will be used to recur [Nick Fury](/card/01084) as much as possible. After that we just try to draw into and play S.i.D.  We don't plan to use our Allies to chump block but most of their stats aren't incredible either, activate them if you need to ping a Tough or finish off a Scheme, otherwise just let them chill off to the side.

We always want to end our turn in [Phased](/card/32031b) form to defend the Villain's activations. Thankfully S.i.D. is not an attack and we can use it when we switch after an Attack. The goal is to stay in Hero form but [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) gives you a chance to flip safetly.

You have good Thwart options but this is probably the deck's weakest link. Best to chip away with basic actions, [Airwalk](/card/32039), and E.V.A., trying to leave S.i.D.s for finishing off Villains and Minions.

decklists.name: Sensational She-Hulk!
decklists.description_md:
I've been enjoying the She-Hulk series, and in honor of its conclusion, here is an X-Men focused **[She-Hulk](/card/10013)** deck! The goal of this deck is to Voltron [She-Hulk](/card/10013) and as many 3+ ATK allies as possible while hitting huge **[Team Strike](/card/32045)s**! While this deck can solo, I highly recommend running it with a co-op partner. Partner deck suggestions at the bottom.
# **Why Shadowcat** - Shadowcat doesn't rely on chump blockers, allowing her to Voltron allies safely - **[Solid](/card/32031a)** can pay for [Team Strike](/card/32045) - Between **[Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037)** and **[Ready to Rumble](/card/32051)** she can guarantee being ready for [Team Strike](/card/32045) - [Team Strike](/card/32045) from **[Phased](/card/32031b)** can bypass guard - As an attack, [Team Strike](/card/32045) lets her flip from [Solid](/card/32031a) to [Phased](/card/32031b) to prepare for the villain phase
The end game for this deck looks like: **[Boot Camp](/card/13016)** and **Uncanny X-Men** (from our multiplayer partner) supports out - **[She-Hulk](/card/10013)** with [Honorary X-Men](/card/33035), [Attack Training](/card/32043), [Enraged](/card/03031) (8 hp, 12 ATK) - **[Wolverine](/card/32041)** with [Attack Training](/card/32043) and [Sidearm](/card/23035) (7 hp, 6 ATK) - **[Thor](/card/25013)** with [Honorary X-Men](/card/33035) and [Attack Training](/card/32043) (7 hp, 5 ATK) - **[Colossus](/card/32048)** with [Honorary X-Men](/card/33035) (5 hp, 4 ATK)
- The upgrades are pretty interchangeable here, the aim being odd-numbered health to give double consequential allies another activation in a pinch. Max copies of **[Honorary X-Men](/card/33035)** are to ease the sequencing of getting [Attack Training](/card/32043) onto [She-Hulk](/card/10013) and [Thor](/card/25013) - [She-Hulk](/card/10013) can hit 13 ATK with **[Sidearm](/card/23035)**, but the ranged is usually better on [Wolverine](/card/32041) since he'll make the most basic attacks. Useful for popping a tough, which would otherwise shut [Team Strike](/card/32045) down. [She-Hulk](/card/10013) will be thwarting more early and should be able to deal with most things with a single attack, making ranged less mandatory. [Team Strike](/card/32045) itself also lets the allies dodge retaliate - **[Enraged](/card/03031)** can be dropped onto any ally to power up [Team Strike](/card/32045) considerably, at the cost of the number of basic attacks that ally can make. Since [She-Hulk](/card/10013) will be thwarting more early game, this hurts her less than it does the others, and late game, it can help her reach her maximum output fast - **[Utopia](/card/33020)** is specifically here to grant +1 ally slot, allowing us to [Team Strike](/card/32045) with 4 allies! - **[Game Time](/card/33022)** is bonkers good. Extra attacks out of all of these 3-12 ATK monsters is huge. Combined with **[X-Mansion](/card/32049)** and more copies of [Game Time](/card/33022) from the partner deck and the damage output is insane. Readying [She-Hulk](/card/10013) for an additional 2-THW can also be handy in a pinch. The heals from [Game Time](/card/33022) and [X-Mansion](/card/32049) stack with the pseudo-heal from [Team Strike](/card/32045) to allow for additional activations when necessary - The deck can get very thin very quickly, helping Shadowcat see [Team Strike](/card/32045), [Game Time](/card/33022), and [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) more often While it is great to demonstrate the ideal set up, most games won't develop this smoothly, nor is it required to be hitting max value to win. Like most of my decks, the ceiling is high, but the floor will still get the job done. Don't be afraid to aggressively use ally health to stabilize the board state! Toughs, [Quick Shift](/card/32040), and [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) should cover defensive needs while building. [She-Hulk](/card/10013), [Airwalk](/card/32039), [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037), and [Wolverine](/card/32041) should cover thwarting needs. Multiplayer is where this deck excels, giving more breathing room to set up these heavy hitter allies in a more fashionable manner. decklists.description_md:

With this deck, I am looking to do 2 things: keep [Rogue](/card/48012) on the table forever, and make a small prefect defense package to use Shadowcat's phased form ability to prevent damage. 

On the first deck pass, I'd focus on getting [Unflappable](/card/09020) and [Rogue](/card/48012) into play, and ideally [Utopia](/card/33020) as well. The goal is to keep Rogue on the table, and provide good allies for her to siphon stats from, namely [Gambit](/card/48021) with a good encounter card, [Rockslide](/card/33013), or [Colossus](/card/32048). Siphoning off of them is an easy 2-3 ATK to defeat minions, and frees up your hero to focus on thwarting and villain damage. I'd also recommend using [Utopia](/card/33020) to ready Rogue, as you have plenty of healing to keep her around and the ready keeps her stats.

The perfect defense package uses [Indomitable](/card/01082) for bankable readies and [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017) for scenarios that need extra thwarting.

The long-term goal is to use ample healing via [Elixir](/card/42011), [Triage](/card/45048), and [Med Team](/card/01080) to keep Rogue alive to keep pumping out damage. Elixir does turn off the extra ally slot from [Utopia](/card/33020), so it is removable if you find you already have enough healing. As a side-package I added [Fighting Fit](/card/16014) to take advantage of any extra healing because I never use it and thought it could be good to take advantage of the resource generation from Solid form. However, Fighting Fit should be a second priority to building your Rogue buffing engine.

decklists.name: Shadowcat
decklists.description_md:
Alter-Ego

Unlike many other X-MEN heroes, [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) does not have many reasons to change form to her alter-ego. If I change her form to her alter-ego it is usually because something went wrong and she needs to recover. The only card in her deck that supports alter-ego is [Kitty's Room](/card/32033). If I changed [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) form to her alter-ego then I usually need to use [Kitty's Room](/card/32033) for some extra healing, even though I prefer to draw a card if I can.

Resources

[Shadowcat](/card/32030a) starts the game with a resource generator for attack or defense events in her [Solid](/card/32031a) upgrade. Her deck also has a resource generator for defense events in her [Nerves of Steel](/card/14017) upgrade. [Deft Focus](/card/16024) reduces the resource cost of SUPERPOWER cards. These are 3 resources that can be used every round. The two [Defensive Energy](/card/32018) cards give [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) a resource that she will want to use for defense events.

Allies

[Shadowcat](/card/32030a) does not need allies, but some allies can certainly improve her deck. Since I am only playing multiplayer and we all use the same limited pool of cards, I lost my wanted allies to the player with the [Colossus](/card/32001a) deck. This is what I was left with. [Colossus](/card/32048) is an ally that I usually remove from this deck because someone else around the table play [Colossus](/card/32001a) hero and I hate that this deck has more than 40 cards. [Lockheed](/card/32032) is usually the only ally I use in this deck. He is cheap and flexible ally that can help [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) with dealing damage or removing threat.

Phased and Confused

The [Phased and Confused](/card/32036) cards are usually used to protect the other players around the table. This card prevents an enemy from attacking, but [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) wants to be attacked and take no damage. Also, the confuse status is mostly to protect other heroes in alter-ego, as [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) rarely change form to her alter-ego when I play her.

Players Phase

Thwart

With 2 thwart and no way in her deck to increase her stats, [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) is no more than decent at thwarting in the early game. At this stage, thwarting is what I do if [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) is ready and already [Phased](/card/32031b) and I do not want to change her mass form. In the late game [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) will have epic rounds like playing [Airwalk](/card/32039) while [Phased](/card/32031b) for 4 thwart, then defend against an attack and takes no damage with 3 copies of [Hard to Ignore](/card/16017) for 3 more thwart. At this stage there will be rounds when [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) will be the best thwarter around the table. [Intangible Interference](/card/32035) will add 2 more thwart as long as there is a scheme with crisis icon in play, but that is very situational and depends on the scenario you play.

Attack

With 2 attack and no way in her deck to increase her stats, [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) is no more than decent at dealing damage in the early game. At this stage, attacking is what I do if [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) is ready and [Solid](/card/32031a) and I want to change her mass form in preparation for the villain phase. The attack cards of this deck somewhat improve the damage output, but the best feature of these attack cards is not their damage output. [Shadowcat Surprise](/card/32037) ready your hero and [Phase Strike](/card/32038) can be used to discard an attachment from an enemy. [Acute Control](/card/32034) will add 2 more points of damage to a minion as long as it has guard or patrol keyword, but that is very situational and depends on the scenario you play.

Villain Phase

[Shadowcat](/card/32030a) may be only a decent superhero during the players phase, but she is the undisputed queen of the villain phase.

Defending You

Your main play happens when an enemy attacks you. [Side Step](/card/14015) and [Preemptive Strike](/card/38015) are the defense cards [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) wants to use when she is [Phased](/card/32031b). They will enable her to defend without exhausting, take no damage, and dealing some damage to the attacker. [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) can also use her basic defend action then use [Ready to Rumble](/card/32051) to ready again.

Defending Others

After [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) defended herself and changed mass form to [Solid](/card/32031a), she still has some options to help defend the other players around the table, or defend herself from another attack. [Counter-Punch](/card/01077) can deal damage to the enemy that just attacked [Shadowcat](/card/32030a), enabling her to change mass form to [Phased](/card/32031b) again for the next defending. [Powerful Punch](/card/32014) and [Shadow and Steel](/card/32050) are both attack and defend cards, enabling [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) to start [Solid](/card/32031a) but be [Phased](/card/32031b) for the defend part. [Quick Shift](/card/32040) is a last resort option. I prefer to use it while [Phased](/card/32031b) and draw two cards, but it is a panic button card when [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) is caught [Solid](/card/32031a).

The Best Offense is a Good Defense

[Change of Fortune](/card/48014) makes [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) wants to deal damage during the villain phase. All of the defend cards in this deck, except [Quick Shift](/card/32040), do just that. Another card that helps [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) deal damage during the villain phase is [Dauntless](/card/16016). I am thinking if I should replace [Dauntless](/card/16016) with [Flow Like Water](/card/26016), but I think that in this deck [Dauntless](/card/16016) is slightly better. Retaliate will trigger when [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) uses her basic defend action, [Flow Like Water](/card/26016) will not.

Draw Cards

I found that after some built up [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) will draw at least one card every villain phase, and you can expect to draw 3-4 cards on a good round. [Unflappable](/card/38013) should draw a card every round. [Change of Fortune](/card/48014) should draw 2 cards often, depending on the scenario you play. [Defensive Energy](/card/32018) will draw a card whenever you use it. [Quick Shift](/card/32040) can draw 2 cards, but I often use it to defend one of the other players around the table. I considered adding [Taunt](/card/42016) for some extra cards drawing. [Shadowcat](/card/32030a) would have no problem dealing with a villain attack for 3 extra cards. Alas, I couldn't find any room for it in the deck.
